body: @jridgewell can you summarize why this strategy for streaming is ideal/optimal for our documentation? Can be bullets too. It's a killer optimization you're adding that is not intuitive
author: jaredpalmer

body:
The is mostly to use the `pull`/`transform` method in `ReadableStream`/`TransformStream`. The old way of using `for await (… of stream)` is eager, meaning we're always trying to process more data and push it into the client stream. But, the client may not need any more data, they may be busy doing their own work with our last chunk.

By switching to `pull`/`transform`, we're able to give control to the consumer. If the consumer doesn't need data, we won't be processing anything. If they do, then `pull`/`transform` will be continually called until a new chunk of data is emitted by our `EventSourceParser`.

I decided not to combine the 2 `TransformerStreams` so that the callback-and-encoding code could be shared between each AI model. They're all doing the exact same thing.

body:
> 2 APIs for this instead of this `mode` stuff: `OpenAITextStream` and `OpenAIDataStream`

Makes sense, agree that's probably easier. Will update.

EDIT: A call to `OpenAIStream(res, { mode: "raw" })` is actually analogous to just `AIStream(res)`, so we don't even need to do that. Apparently it's redundant to wrap with `AIStream()` at all if you have a ReadableStream already, just return new `Response(res)`.

There will ultimately end up being more modes than just raw/text though.
author: ctjlewis

body:
@jaredpalmer I added completion JSON parsing to demonstrate, and converted this to a draft for now. 

The mode is just a way to switch between chunk parsers. You can see how this pattern lets you do `OpenAIStream(res, { mode: "json" })` or wrap whatever you want with `AIStream(res, { mode, parsers: ... })`. This can easily be extended to better integration with [OpenAI Function Calling](https://openai.com/blog/function-calling-and-other-api-updates) or JSON-like prompt responses.

body:
> > It would be nice to parse the response from OpenAI differently, when it comes to function calling. Since it won't be a stream response. 🤔
> 
> Function calling responses are streamable too. Furthermore, especially if the `function_call` parameter is set to `auto` in the request, you don't know whether or not the model will decide to call a function, so the streaming utils must be updated to support streaming the function calls to the clients as well.

I mean, don't get my wrong, it's nice that we could stream function call responses, but I guess if we do that, we could break the SRP (Single-responsibility principle).

Consider this, for example, the Open API payload endpoint, accepts an `stream`  parameter which is boolean. 
If this parameter is false, we may don't want to parse the response as `stream`, We can stop that logic at that moment, and parse the response differently. We can also add support to useChat or any other interface for the user to choose when they would like streamed responses or not. In my head, this new function calling functionality is 3 additional steps in the middle of the flow. That is:

- Seeing if finish_reason is 'function_call' ( 99,99% yes, depending on your software design)
- Call your function
- Call again the API with the function results with role='function'

Then, resume the streaming flow. 
But, I may be wrong in my point of view, anyways, I'm trying to reason about it, together.

If you look at my [comment explaining how function calling chunks are streamed](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ai/pull/178/files#diff-b4fc3cf85f3dc974899314160d4930248499e7e5c371f123d4d9a4948c6b3e62R14) or my [test data showing the chunks](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ai/pull/178/files#diff-c386744b666862eb2649d1936a536bc75686a61b0d5a4d9c243a303fd765907fR64), you can see that the function call name is not at risk of being malformed, but the function call "arguments" can be malformed JSON (or improperly escaped), so my PR leaves the arguments as a string, and leaves it to the client to handle the case where OpenAI returns malformed JSON in the arguments.

body:
Take https://github.com/vercel-labs/ai/issues/205#issuecomment-1603437504 as an example. Let's say we wanted to stream both the responses.

in first chain

```
Tragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a story of love, loss, and redemption. It follows the story of two young lovers, Jack and Jill, who meet on a beach at sunset. They quickly fall in love and plan to spend the rest of their lives together. \n\nHowever, tragedy strikes when Jack is killed in a car accident. Jill is left devastated and unable to cope with the loss of her beloved. She spirals into a deep depression and begins to lose hope. \n\nJust when all seems lost, Jill discovers that Jack had left her a letter before his death. In the letter, he tells her that he will always love her and that she should never give up hope. With this newfound strength, Jill is able to find the courage to move on with her life and find happiness again. \n\nTragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a story of love, loss, and redemption. It is a story of hope and courage in the face of tragedy. It is a story of finding strength in the darkest of times and of never giving up.",     
```

handleChainEnd gets called, stream is closed. Second chain can't write the second response

```
Tragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a powerful and moving story of love, loss, and redemption. The play follows the story of two young lovers, Jack and Jill, whose plans for a future together are tragically cut short when Jack is killed in a car accident. \n\nThe play is beautifully written and the performances are outstanding. The actors bring a depth of emotion to their characters that is both heartbreaking and inspiring. The story is full of unexpected twists and turns, and the audience is taken on an emotional rollercoaster as Jill struggles to come to terms with her loss. \n\nThe play is ultimately a story of hope and resilience, and it is sure to leave audiences with a newfound appreciation for life and love. Tragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a must-see for anyone looking for an emotionally charged and thought-provoking experience."
```

There's probably many ways to fix this, but the way I suggested in this PR seems to work for most use cases I've tried.

body:
Thanks for the work on this. I'm going to try out function calling and so may not need to stream extra data.

However I've been thinking about DX and have an idea: I think the core data of RAG apps is not a _message_ log, it's an _event_ log containing user messages, function calls, function responses, and assistant messages. A RAG app needs to present views of that event log to both the user and the assistant; the assistant's view is a message log, and the user's view is whatever JSON drives their UI. The current API (pre-experimental_streamData), which thinks of things as OpenAI-style message logs rather than generic event logs, makes it hard to handle those two different views of the data.

For example, in my RAG app I want my search results to be formatted as a plaintext system message for the OpenAI message array, but want to view those same results as JSON client side, so that I can present a "related research" UI section. Under the current functionCalling API that might involve parsing system messages client side, which is unwieldy. With the current streamData API that would involve interleaving the data array back into my message history as system messages, which is also a bit awkward. Either that or duplicating data as system messages AND streamData.

So I think my ideal API would be to have a generic type called "event" that looks something like this:
```typescript
type Event<T> = {
  name: string // or generic string literal
  data: T
}
```
This `Event` type would be part of message history, and I would set up functions on client and server side to determine how to map that event to a system message for OpenAI, and how to interpret the event data as UI client side.

This is a bit different from message-correlated data, since the data event is a neighboring member in the message/event array rather than an additional field of a message. I think that's more sensible, since fundamentally the data event has its own chronological place in the stream, you can even think of a data event as a message from a 3rd party agent, like a 'search agent' who just sent a message to the stream.

Curious to hear people's thoughts on this!

body:
@peterdresslar Can you provide an example? Steps I used to reproduce (and fix) the error locally: 1. Clone https://github.com/ctate/vercel-ai (my fork) 2. Checkout the `issue-567` branch via `git checkout issue-567` 3. Run `pnpm install && pnpm run build` 4. Run the "next-openai" example: `pnpm --filter=next-openai run dev` 5. Add some debugging code in `examples/next-openai/app/page.tsx` like `{error &&
{error.message}
}` Then, to test, I simply opened localhost:3000, turned wifi off, asked a question, and saw the error. Then I turned wifi back on and asked another question. The error disappeared and I got a result back. (before the fix, the error never went away) The event loop for handleSubmit is `handleSubmit()` > `append()` > `triggerRequest()`. `triggerRequest()` is also called via `reload()`. In both scenarios, `triggerRequest()` seems like a good place to clear the error because `triggerRequest()` is also the only place where an error is set (it's also the same function that changes the `isLoading` state). Lmk if this helps. Thanks!

`useAssistant` is on the client side. The goal is that all assistant based-behavior can run on the server side, without any client involvement. The client is only notified with information that could lead to rendering changes (e.g. progress information, streaming messages in the future, etc.)

Can you point to the exact while loop? Please note that a) the server side implementation is an example, any production system would use something way more complex to guarantee resiliency, failover, etc., and b) most of the code has async calls.

I see. Does anyone know if there is a way to return the function call decision to the? In the example, the model in the backend has access to the function call and function call return stuff but the frontend doesn't have access to it. Basically i'd like the frontend to know what function have been called and what is it's return value.

Line 97-104 of this [file](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/5f4115bdbba7a7fcaae15879b421a41b20620c2c/examples/next-openai/app/api/chat-with-tools/route.ts#L97)
author: frmsaul

body:
You can return a string from the function call on the server and that will get sent to the client as a standard message.  So you could do something like 
```javascript
      return JSON.stringify({function: toolCall.func.name, result: 'Handled'});
```
And then look for json formatted messages in the client.

If you want to return a function response to the API, (like the current weather) for the model to interpret and also tell the client that the function was handled, you might be able to get clever by adding some sort of `modelGotFunctionReturn` function on the client side where you tell the model to tell you about functions that were handled.  Not sure if that would work, but might be worth a try.

If none of that works, you could look into
https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/5f4115bdbba7a7fcaae15879b421a41b20620c2c/packages/core/streams/openai-stream.ts#L673
and see if there is some changes you could make to add the functionality you are looking for.

I've been away from this code for a bit so I don't have too much more to offer than that.  Although, there is a draft PR up with some changes to that code that you could also look into for handing some calls on the server and others on the client.
https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/1123

As per the OpenAI API docs, there should be a `JSON.parse(tool.function.arguments)` I actually ran into this in a different project I was working on so I did a ` if typeof arguments === "string" ? body:
Thanks sm for working on this.

When you say "parallel client/server tool calls", would it also support one either: (1) allowing a server-side tool call to call a client-side tool, or (2) passing the result of a server-side tool to the client?

I've been trying to find a workable impl for either of the two above scenarios, but the closest thing I've seen is serializing the result of server-side tool calls via JSON and sending it back as an assistant message, which comes w/ its own set of caveats like the lack of a follow-up message from the assistant w/o an additional user message.
author: rajdtta

body:
> When you say "parallel client/server tool calls", would it also support one either: (1) allowing a server-side tool call to call a client-side tool, or (2) passing the result of a server-side tool to the client?

It will support both client and server side tool calls, and they can be mixed and parallel.

### Example

You define 2 tools, one that is executed client side (i.e. has no execute method), and one that is executed server-side (i.e. with an execute method). The client side code then receives 3 related events:

- tool call for client side tool
- tool call for server side tool
- tool result for server side tool

On the client, you'd execute the client-side tool, do whatever you want with the server side tool result, and then use onFinish to send back both tool results to the server, so that the AI can continue the conversation (this is important for this to work at all, because OpenAI expects tool results for all tool calls it invokes). 

On the next roundtrip, the LLM will know the tool results and can come up with text responses or more tool calls.

Please note that this is a WIP and the design might change.

And the way we handle the 2nd invocation flow is now when the `Message` that's passed to `onFinish` contains `toolInvocation` results, we call `experimental_addToolResult`, for both client and server tools?
> 
> How do we send back the tool results to the LLM in the server-side tool case without direct access to `triggerRequest` - or does `experimental_addToolResult` handle de-duplicating the `toolInvocation` results array and we can do something like this:
> 
> ```
>   // handle sending response of server-side tool back to LLM
>   
>   const { experimental_addToolResult } = useChat({
>     ....
>     onFinish: async (message) => {
>       if (
>         message.role === 'assistant' &&
>         message.toolInvocations &&
>         message.toolInvocations.every(
>           (toolInvocation) => 'result' in toolInvocation,
>         )
>       ) {
>         return message.toolInvocations.forEach((toolInvocation) => {
>           if ('result' in toolInvocation) {
>             experimental_addToolResult({
>               result: toolInvocation.result,
>               toolCallId: toolInvocation.toolCallId,
>             })
>           }
>         })
>       }
> 
>       return onFinish(message)
>     },
>   ...
>   })
> ```

From my understanding, `experimental_addToolResult` is used to pipe back results from client tool invocations back to the LLM (so that it's able to interpret the results and use it to decide its next step).

As for having the LLM interpret server-side tool calls, that's something I'm still trying to figure out in my sandbox. Quickly subbing in the snippet you sent above just causes the model to repeatedly call the server tool in a loop, and trying to use `append` to add a user message makes the model trigger a duplicate tool call (but interestingly, the result of the duplicate/second tool call doesn't get appended to the toolInvocation object despite it executing on the server-side).

body:
> Question in a different context: Is there a business process that must be followed to add a provider to the AI ​​SDK document?

If you mean 3rd party providers, it depends. We will probably maintain the ones for the big cloud providers and large LLM providers in our repo (e.g. Bedrock, Azure OpenAI). For other providers you can publish them as community providers in your own repo and we are more than happy to list them under community providers, see https://sdk.vercel.ai/providers/community-providers

body:
I had the same requirement and ended up building a layer on top of streamText to do it. It sounds like this will be natively supported in the SDK at some point, but for the time being I think it's still something one needs to put together oneself.

Check out https://github.com/edspencer/stream-multi if you are interested - the little video there shows the ability to have the LLM respond with both streaming text and any number of tools calls.

I published it as a npm module called [ai-stream-multi](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ai-stream-multi?activeTab=readme). It basically has the same API as streamText(), but adds the concept of `Segments`, which are either a Tool or Text, and of which there can be any number in a given response from the LLM. Use the `onSegment` callback to update the AIState.

![Demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edspencer/stream-multi/main/demo.gif)

body: Was there a reason why the completion model provider needed to be copied (vs tweaking the OpenAI completion provider and reusing it)?
author: lgrammel

body:
Mostly that was in the event to prepare for cases that Azure's formatting differs from OpenAI's.

One major difference that didn't make it easy to just pull in is the difference between [`OpenAIChatConfig`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/68ececdbd02135f8d08e84e3a455d4cafa4ec0d7/packages/openai/src/openai-chat-language-model.ts#L27-L33) and [`OpenAICompletionConfig`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/68ececdbd02135f8d08e84e3a455d4cafa4ec0d7/packages/openai/src/openai-completion-language-model.ts#L27-L33) since they are constructed differently.

If you'd like, I can try to patch the [`openai-completion-language-model.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/68ececdbd02135f8d08e84e3a455d4cafa4ec0d7/packages/openai/src/openai-completion-language-model.ts#L27-L33) to keep it consistent? Otherwise the constructor is different, and I have to make a new `azure-openai-completion-language-model`.

---
For example:

I can't pull in: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/68ececdbd02135f8d08e84e3a455d4cafa4ec0d7/packages/openai/src/openai-completion-language-model.ts#L15-L25 directly from `@ai-sdk/openai` as the `@ai-sdk/azure` package, which makes adding our own  `azure-openai-completion-language-model` without copying additional ones difficult, as otherwise I have to do relative imports like this, as they aren't exposed in `@ai-sdk/openai/internal`:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/c4abd0f37d9605cb69660e5406b5026b5ee0130f/packages/azure/src/azure-openai-completion-language-model.ts#L15-L17

---
c4abd0f37d9605cb69660e5406b5026b5ee0130f is a commit with reduced copied code, only adding [`packages/azure/src/azure-openai-completion-language-model.ts`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/c4abd0f37d9605cb69660e5406b5026b5ee0130f/packages/azure/src/azure-openai-completion-language-model.ts), but adding imports from `@ai-sdk/openai/src` directly to keep `createCompletionModel` consistent with `createChatModel` in the `azure-openai-provider`.

e5319005c2adf78ce41bcbf0cdaa926f10332637 is a commit with most of the code copied over.

Please let me know which one is optimal, and I'll clean that up.

---
Finally, I can't get the test deployment to do anything with the completion model, so https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/5cd6c6d3fa5e3c155b10d3c17eca6deab719bcba/packages/azure/src/azure-openai-provider.test.ts#L61-L125 will likely fail.

I was wondering if there's a way to get this into the official package. Because claude has one of the top ai models, and vertex is an ai platform from google. Obviously, many people will be waiting to see this work.

In the case of Azure OpenAI and OpenAI, it's possible to get them to work under the same package since they don't require additional dependencies. [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76711533/how-to-use-the-python-openai-client-with-both-azure-and-openai-at-the-same-time)](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76711533/how-to-use-the-python-openai-client-with-both-azure-and-openai-at-the-same-time))

For anthropic using vertex, it requires the google auth library, which is irrelevant to include in a package used by users who only access the Anthropic endpoint.

If anybody is getting this issue: ``` ts: Type '"auto" | { type: string; toolName: string; }' is not assignable to type 'ToolChoice<{ createDocument: Tool; }, "strip", ZodTypeAny, { title: string; kind: "text" | ... 2 more ... | "sheet"; }, { ...; }>, { ...; }> & { ...; }; updateDocument: Tool<...> & { ...; }; requestSuggestions: Tool<...> & { ...; }; }> |...'. Type '{ type: string; toolName: string; }' is not assignable to type 'ToolChoice<{ createDocument: Tool; }, "strip", ZodTypeAny, { title: string; kind: "text" | ... 2 more ... | "sheet"; }, { ...; }>, { ...; }> & { ...; }; updateDocument: Tool<...> & { ...; }; requestSuggestions: Tool<...> & { ...; }; }> |...'. Type '{ type: string; toolName: string; }' is not assignable to type '{ type: "tool"; toolName: "createDocument" | "updateDocument" | "requestSuggestions"; }'. Types of property 'type' are incompatible. Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"tool"'. ``` You can fix it like this: ```ts const toolChoice = shouldCreateDocument ? { type: 'tool' as const, toolName: 'createDocument' as const } : 'auto'; ```

body:
Hey thanks for the contribution! 

It's an important addition and I've considered this implementation path. However, **I do not want to add a provider-specific mechanism that is likely to change in the future to CoreMessage**. Instead I plan to add a mechanism that will let us add provider-specific features without affecting the core message. 

You can find a prototype for anthropic caching here that uses the `providerMetadata` mechanism to limit this feature to the Anthropic provider: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/2678

body:
Thanks @blechatellier for the PR. I think the overall solution for deciding what to do on each roundtrip (esp. with server side roundtrips) is more complex, e.g. prompt changes and full state machines need to be considered. Including your solution into the API would mean we need to maintain and extend it, and coordinate how it works with said future features. I would therefore prefer not to include it in the AI SDK.

Can you achieve the same by using tools without an `execute` function? Or by setting roundtrips to `0` in `useChat` (easier now that we have server-side roundtrips in `streamText`)?
author: lgrammel

body:
@lgrammel no worries - I'll close this. Thanks for implementing the roundtrips on the server side; they're very useful. I'm still figuring out how to best implement a simple use case where you can conditionally switch between different instructions within the same LLM call (e.g., drafting an email vs. answering a question) and render a different UI on the client. This is something I've been able to do easily with createStreamableUI and nested LLM calls but not with streamText. I’m attempting to replicate this with tools, but I feel it might be an anti-pattern.

Are you still considering enabling nested calls within a tool and streaming the result? https://github.com/vercel/ai/discussions/2666#discussioncomment-10473634

body:
> Hey @tonyfarney meant to come back to this - the issue is legit, but I need to verify this fix actually works in different settings, e.g.. when something is already non-empty or when there are non-changes for non-empty data.

Looking the code, the only situation data is not an empty array when passed to `onUpdate` is in `process-data-protocol-response.ts`:
```typescript
update([...previousMessages, ...merged], [...data]); // make a copy of the data array
```
I think it's possible the situation of calling the `update` callback for the exact same `data`. But for avoiding to mutate stream data in such situation, would be necessary to compare the arrays or maybe just to check the array length.

body:
The main idea is that libraries like the Vercel AI SDK implement [Standard Schema](https://github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema) to easily support any schema that follows that spec. This simplifies and improves the DX and both sides. Library authors are no longer required to understand and implement a specific schema library, and in the worst case, maintain a bunch of adapters in their own source code. Users, on the other hand, no longer need to wrap their schema in an adapter function to make it compatible.

The Vercel AI SDK could allow JSON schema and standard schema as input for the `parameters` property. If the input contains a `"~standard"` key, it can be passed to the `standardSchema` function to format it to a unified schema interface.
author: fabian-hiller

body: Great initiative on the **StandardSchema**. This is definitely the way forward as it massively reduces implementation overhead while increasing interoperability.
author: MentalGear

body: @fabian-hiller I really like the idea. However, until standard schema supports conversion to JSON schema and potentially OpenAPI schema, it is only a half-way solution for the needs of the AI SDK (tool calling, structured outputs). We would still need dependencies to the json schema converters, which in turn will have dependencies on the libraries. I'll think more about how to apply it to the AI SDK.
author: lgrammel

body: Indeed I would assume for JSON export to be next on the task list for standard schema since it's the most universal and would also give an additional incentive for other validation lib authors to use standard schema and get JSON export for free.
author: MentalGear

body: Yes, in general it is a good idea to add it to the Standard Schema spec, but there is one drawback and that is the bundle size. Being forced to add our `toJsonSchema` function to every schema is probably not an option for Valibot, because we need a tree-shakable solution to not unnecessary increase the bundle size of every schema if this functionality is never used.

body:
Notes:
- @lgrammel how would you typically test this in a deployment? I'm not sure of the best way to build and include local modifications to the SDK packages. I played around with `pnpm pack` but you must have some standard relatively straightforward approach I imagine. I was testing manually with a trivial `examples` I added, but of course it pulls the published SDK on deploy. Just asking for my knowledge for the future (does not block PR per se)
- `loadOptionalSetting` is dead code after this PR but feels useful enough, likely to be used in the future, to leave around (but happy to remove it if you prefer)
- we could as discussed in the issue alternately prefix with `AI_SDK_` and/or remove the other defaults as well, but this PR seemed most reasonable on some reflection (as noted in docs/comments)
- there are not currently unit tests for the involved provider code, I'd be happy to add some to validate the env var use (and non-use) if it feels worthwhile but it's a pretty small change
author: shaper

body:
It occurred to me to check the other `AWS_XXX` default env vars in a clean deployment and I found that they're actually set as well (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`) so I am now inclined to remove these from use as defaults as well and update the documentation to explain. At least this would make the bedrock provider consistent in not using the AWS env var defaults.

Rationale is to minimize the risk of developer surprise due to unintentional creds conflict.

I realize that this is effectively known and documented behavior: https://vercel.com/guides/how-can-i-use-aws-sdk-environment-variables-on-vercel however my understanding is that devs are likely to set up separate creds and aim to use those, and doing so while omitting some values risks defaulting to these against developer intent.

Alternate (this is my current thinking pending your feedback): we can leave logic to use defaults as it is at ToT (no code changes), and just update documentation to note that these vars are sometimes pre-populated, are used as defaults, and devs should either use `bedrockOptions` to avoid defaults or make sure they review their environment variable values (and/or pass `undefined`, etc. for values to omit as needed) if they experience credential failures.

Let me know your thoughts.
author: shaper

body:
My main concern (and that's why I've been holding off here) is that this will be a breaking change that renders some working setups non-functional.

I see two options:
- we add documentation about the current behavior and workaround (short-term preferred)
- we make breaking change and do a major version bump. In this case we want to get the overall design right - which may mean no environment variables and also renaming/adjust how we use `bedrockOptions`. The goal of environment variables was making the local development easy to get started with, but it seems to be too confusing for deployment.

Re smaller comments:
- re testing: ideally we'd test it but it may not be possible in all cases
- re dead code: agree to leave it in, at least for now
- re prefixing: would like to discuss separately
- re unit tests: don't feel strong about unit tests here, the main risk is having a design that minimized setup issues in AWS environments, not bugs in the code

If you'd rather skip all updates until the next major or minor version, let me know by commenting `@dependabot ignore this major version` or `@dependabot ignore this minor version`. You can also ignore all major, minor, or patch releases for a dependency by adding an [`ignore` condition](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/configuration-options-for-dependency-updates#ignore) with the desired `update_types` to your config file.

If you change your mind, just re-open this PR and I'll resolve any conflicts on it.

You can also ignore all major, minor, or patch releases for a dependency by adding an [`ignore` condition](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/configuration-options-for-dependency-updates#ignore) with the desired `update_types` to your config file.

body:
The implementation itself looks very good. However, at this point I'm not sure if we want to add reranking models to the AI SDK, because it increases the API surface that we need to manage, and I haven't gotten a chance to look at the different providers to understand what a common, stable API would look like.

What major providers other than Cohere offer re-ranking? I'm very hesitant to add any abstraction that is based on a single provider implementation.
author: lgrammel

body:
Thank you for the feedback! 

Major providers offering reranking capabilities:

1. **Cohere**: Reranking API
   - Docs: https://docs.cohere.com/v1/reference/rerank

2. **Together AI**
   - Docs: https://docs.together.ai/reference/rerank-1

3. **Voyage AI**: [Specialized reranking models](https://blog.voyageai.com/2024/09/30/rerank-2/) 
   - Docs: https://docs.voyageai.com/reference/reranker-api

4. **MixedBread AI**: Reranking endpoint
   - Docs: https://www.mixedbread.ai/api-reference/endpoints/reranking
   
5. **Jina AI**
   - Docs: https://api.jina.ai/redoc#tag/rerank/operation/rank_v1_rerank_post
 

These providers share common patterns in their APIs:
- Input: Array of documents + query
- Similar parameters (top_k/n, return_documents/input)
- Output: Reranked indices with relevance scores
author: patelvivekdev

body:
Adding reranking support enhances the SDK's RAG capabilities:

1. **Complete RAG Pipeline**:
   - Current: Embeddings + LLMs
   - With Reranking: Embeddings → Reranking → LLMs
   - Improves relevance of context before LLM processing

2. **Enhanced Semantic Search**:
   - After vector similarity search via embeddings
   - Reranking refines results for better accuracy
   - Critical for high-precision information retrieval
   
This addition would give developers a complete, production-ready RAG solution within the SDK.
author: patelvivekdev

body:
This PR causes an (i believe) unintended side-effect, changing the `createdAt` type from `Date` to `string`.

**Implications:**
* Might cause runtime errors for users, e.g. `message.createdAt.getTime()`
* With typings still bound to `Date`, there won't be any eslint/ts warnings.

**Recommentation:**

```ts
const copiedMessage = {
  ...JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(currentMessage)),
  createdAt: currentMessage.createdAt, // <- NEW, to retain correct type of `createdAt`
  revisionId: generateId2()
};
```
author: tobiasstrebitzer

body:
👀 

This looks interesting! I would honestly still rather just have the ability to catch the full response from the LLM provider and have the flexibility to deal with things however I want. Abstractions and helpers like this are awesome, but if we can _only_ access the provider response through these then the SDK starts to feel rigid / over abstracted. I think having both is the best case though - an easy helper for those who want to use it, but ultimately flexibility for someone who needs to do something more custom.

I would love to know where your head is regarding my last comment on #3779, I am happy to put in a PR to expose the full provider response on the error object if you are aligned. Thanks!
author: williamlmao

body:
@williamlmao the approach that you propose has several limitations / downsides:

a) full responses are not always available (streaming, or providers w/o api calls)
b) for correct multi-step behavior, the error recovery / tool call repair needs to be handled inside generateText/streamText
c) exposing provider-specific results needs to dependencies that the AI SDK is trying to abstract, namely code that relies on provider-specific details

I want to explore tool call repair first (and if it works structured output repair as well), before looking into a more provider specific approach if needed. My hunch is that tool call repair & structured output repair will end up being sufficient and better integrated.

author: lgrammel
ShervK

body:
> Thanks for the feedback, I didn't realize there were plans to implement token based auth for google vertex as well.
> 
> One idea that comes to mind is setting up a type-based approach for providers that have multiple auth methods, something like
> 
> ```ts
> type AuthenticationMethod = 
>   | { type: 'apiKey'; value: string }
>   | { type: 'bearer'; tokenProvider: () => Promise<string> }
>   | { type: 'custom'; getAuth: () => Promise<Record<string, string>> };
> ```
> 
> You could still have `apiKey` as an option and default to that if its provided, as to not cause breaking changes. Would this be more along the lines of what you're looking for?

Hi, thanks for the contribution, I will take a closer look at it!

A question: all of the above seem effectively implementable if we expose a way to optionally add to request headers. We have one today via `headers` in provider settings today, however, it isn't async, which can limit what one might need to do (e.g. fetching/refreshing an auth token with its own async ops needed). We could add a new one that allows async.

That has a nice feel from a simplicity of API surface perspective as it's one thing to think about, though it's also admittedly a little raw, as not all devs or docs want to think about or deal with talking about headers vs. the auth primitives/methods.

A concern could be any performance impact/overhead from calling the dev-provided headers population (do we do it once and cache it, or on each request, or catch auth errors and try refreshing by calling it again, ...). I expect we already have this auth-lifetime issue in some cases, and I wonder whether folks are having to catch auth timeout/failure and re-create the provider with updated auth in some cases.

Stepping back -- today I theorize you actually can already do what you want by calling your identity token provider before you create the Azure provider, getting your token, and then using the existing `headers` settings. The issues I can see you'd face, per the above, are (1) a little less semantically-relevant API for Azure (others would have to know to do similarly, we'd want to enhance docs/examples), and (2) any token timeout/refresh issues. Is this accurate, am I missing anything, what else comes to mind?

It would be great to hear your thoughts on the above.
author: shaper

body:
@shaper Those are great points and you nailed the main challenges here.

I actually thought about using `getHeaders` for this PR at first, but the async nature of token providers is what stopped me. Since `getHeaders` is used consistently across providers, I didn’t want to break a standard just for this feature. That said, an async `getHeaders` would be a great way to clean this up and keep things consistent across providers if thats an option. 

Initially, I had token auth working by setting it up in the `headers` option at the request level. I ran into issues with token lifetimes when using `headers` at the provider level since the provider had to be configured ahead of time (I'm using `customProvider`). As the project grew and we started using more providers, it got trickier to manage for the reasons you brought up (caching, validating, refetching). That’s when I started looking into how client libraries (like OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) handle token-based auth. Most of them seem to fetch a fresh token on each request, which avoids those lifetime issues.
Right around that time, you rolled out the custom fetch feature for providers so I used that to fetch a new token on each request, mimicking the behaviour of those libraries.

You can achieve this with what's available in the SDK right now, but it's not as intuitive as other libraries, and like you said, "a little raw". I was hoping to help bridge that gap, but I agree that the docs could address this just as well. I’ve actually seen a few comments from people saying they can’t use the SDK because of its missing native token-based auth support for their cloud provider. I’ve also heard similar feedback in enterprise settings. So, even if this PR doesn’t move forward, adding an example in the docs for token-based auth would go a long way toward helping folks out.

I’m happy to tweak this further or help with the docs if that’s the way to go
author: ShervK

body:
Hi @shaper 

I saw the PRs for the Resolvable utility type and Vertex AI auth changed get merged. I'll get to work on changing this PR to use those standards. 

I saw that the Vertex auth implementation used the `google-auth-library` package and added authentication options to the provider settings, is this something you want to see in the Azure provider? [`@azure/identity`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/sdk/identity/identity/README.md) supports a lot of different [credential methods](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/sdk/identity/identity/README.md#credential-classes) so native support would cause the provider to balloon in size. 
An easier approach would be updating the docs with a section about using [`getBearerTokenProvider`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/@azure/identity/?view=azure-node-latest#@azure-identity-getbearertokenprovider) function included in `@azure/identity` to retrieve the token using the user's preferred credential method and adding the token to the Resolvable Header.

I can support both implementations, let me know which sounds better.
author: ShervK

body:
> Hi @shaper
> 
> I saw the PRs for the Resolvable utility type and Vertex AI auth changed get merged. I'll get to work on changing this PR to use those standards.
> 
> I saw that the Vertex auth implementation used the `google-auth-library` package and added authentication options to the provider settings, is this something you want to see in the Azure provider? [`@azure/identity`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/sdk/identity/identity/README.md) supports a lot of different [credential methods](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/blob/main/sdk/identity/identity/README.md#credential-classes) so native support would cause the provider to balloon in size. An easier approach would be updating the docs with a section about using [`getBearerTokenProvider`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/javascript/api/@azure/identity/?view=azure-node-latest#@azure-identity-getbearertokenprovider) function included in `@azure/identity` to retrieve the token using the user's preferred credential method and adding the token to the Resolvable Header.
> 
> I can support both implementations, let me know which sounds better.

The easier approach and keeping the provider lighter weight sounds better to me. If you put together a draft PR we'd be happy to look at it and discuss, that would be great, thanks!

There were two reasons we kept the google-auth-library for vertex:
- backwards-compatibility (folks were already using it) which is something we care about a lot
- DX, it's really nice having the one-line import of the default vertex provider instance "just work"

The last point is a down side of the simpler approach. I think you'll end up with something that's like at least 4 lines or so wherever someone creates a provider instance.

Let's see what it looks like when you try it? My only other idea, if we want to pursue the goal of lighter-weight providers, is to have a separate contrib-type package where small hooks like this can live and folks could leverage that way, and we can push heavyweight deps to those other more specific packages that depend on the provider. I am not saying we should do this yet, it's just the only thing that comes to mind. Maybe you'll find something else syntactic-sugar-wise etc.

The docs are based on our (working) Nuxt example, see e.g. here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/nuxt-openai/server/api/chat.ts

That being said, I like having `OPENAI_API_KEY` better - but I want to keep all docs consistent, and also follow Nuxt best practices. What are the Nuxt best practices for naming such API keys in env variables?

body:
Hi there, thank you for the contribution! As you may have seen, we recently shipped a 2.0 update to the `google-vertex` provider:

https://x.com/aisdk/status/1866044262409765270

As part of this we moved to using the Vertex AI Gemini REST API instead of the `google-cloud/vertex` package. It is likely pretty straightforward to add it using REST instead.

Just looking briefly at the example on the page you linked it looks like the submitted audio would be handled as a file attachment, which we already have support for, so I am not sure we need the `cachedContent` setting. We would need a way to add the `"generatationConfig": { "audioTimestamp": true }`. I think this would require using `experimental_providerMetadata` to tag the message with the file, and then in message conversion or just outside of it we'd add it to the request as needed. @lgrammel may have further thoughts.

We would need unit tests for new logic, demo scripts in `examples/ai-core/src/{generate,stream}Text` with a sample audio snippet, and added test cases similarly for generate/stream in the `examples/ai-core/src/e2e/google-vertex.test.ts` file.

If this sounds like a lot we can put it in our feature request queue, please file an issue or link to one if it already exists.
author: shaper

While it's unlikely for embedding models to directly result in an empty vector or a zero vector, during testing I accidentally created two empty vectors, causing cosineSimilarity to return NaN.

I've changed it to return 0, but I think it might make more sense to throw an error, as errors can be caught.

Keeping the original behavior, or adding this change might not make a big difference for mostly systems.

body:
Hi there, thank you for the PR! We are in the midst of reworking the bedrock provider (if curious, see https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4582) to remove the dependency on the Bedrock SDK, and so the smithy-based middleware hook will go away.

I think we can achieve your goal of adding to headers through a more standard AI SDK pattern:
- add a provider setting to allow specifying a function that produces headers
- at request time, this function is called and given a chance to produce whatever add'l headers it would like to add
- internally in the current provider, we essentially do what you have done here

The goal is to avoid exposing the bedrock-client or the middleware reference directly, since those will be going away, while still providing a way to add to the headers on each request.

You can see an example where we use this pattern with the Google Vertex provider calling into the Google GenAI language model code, ref: [1](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/3551c1df311c99613f6399366f316181a1225d28/packages/google-vertex/src/google-vertex-provider.ts#L67), [2](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts#L34), [3](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts#L213).

I can take your PR and evolve it to reflect the above, would that meet your needs?

body:
Thanks for your patience -- we are close to landing https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/4582 which will have `headers` support as discussed, along with a rewrite to use REST instead of the bedrock client library.

If you'd like to try it out early there is a snapshot release version of `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` from yesterday `0.0.0-c0cd7082-20250211021941` which I've tested with `ai` `4.1.25`.

The one thing to be aware of migration-wise is that we've removed `bedrockOptions` from the provider settings, and so you need to pass credential related settings directly in the provider settings. You may need to set unused credential settings e.g. `sessionToken` to `undefined` if for example they pick up any env vars defined by your containing runtime (serverless fns, for example, may have `AWS_xxx` defined even if you don't yourself).

I expect we will publish a proper release of the new version in the next day or two, so more than fine to just wait, but I didn't want to leave you hanging without an update. We're almost there, and would welcome your feedback once you do get a chance to try the new thing.

Hey team, 

Although this looks great as the Bedrock AI SDK has less external dependencies, the new update makes this new package super limited. For instance, we rely on [Vercel OIDC](https://vercel.com/docs/security/secure-backend-access/oidc/aws) to connect securely to our AWS Backend which the new package does not support.

What is the potential way forward?

For instance, we rely on [Vercel OIDC](https://vercel.com/docs/security/secure-backend-access/oidc/aws) to connect securely to our AWS Backend which the new package does not support.
> 
> What is the potential way forward?

Hi there, @meleksomai in case it is helpful please take a look at https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/2780#issuecomment-2660787835 which shows how aws sso and a range of other creds files/locations/etc. can be used.

I will look more closely at OIDC specifically, but on initial read it looks like a similar approach would work, just revising my example at above link to use `awsCredentialsProvider` instead.

Let us know if this works for you. I plan to update the Bedrock docs to describe these alternate authentication approaches soon.

I'm getting the following (expected) typescript error:

![CleanShot 2025-02-10 at 09 17 16](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38c113af-61f9-4a26-bcb2-3918938deb99)

`AttributeValue` comes from OTEL and does not support `null`: 

`export declare type AttributeValue = string | number | boolean | Array<null | undefined | string> | Array<null | undefined | number> | Array<null | undefined | boolean>;`

https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/blob/main/api/src/common/Attributes.ts#L35

I'm trying to understand the request here. Do you want us to support `null` (which is not supported by OTEL)?
author: lgrammel

body: I really appreciate the thought and effort that has gone into maintaining this library—thank you for your time and for engaging in this discussion. The current approach works well for strictly typed TypeScript codebases, but in practice, many real-world projects either don’t use TypeScript or don’t enforce strict types across their entire codebase. Because of that, it would be ideal if passing `null` as a metadata property didn’t result in an error. Right now, the library already allows `undefined` values, even though the OTEL `AttributeValue` documentation suggests they shouldn’t be permitted: From what I see, there are three potential paths forward: 1️⃣ **Leave it as-is**, requiring consumers of the library to manually filter out `null` values before passing attributes, which could lead to unexpected crashes if they don’t. 2️⃣ **Merge this PR** and handle `null` values safely rather than throwing an error, similar to how `undefined` values are already treated. We could also log a warning to inform users that `null` attributes are being ignored if that is desired. 3️⃣ **Remove `undefined` from the attributes type** to better align with OTEL requirements, though this would be a breaking change. I personally think option 2 is the most pragmatic approach since it prevents unexpected crashes while maintaining flexibility for different use cases. I’d love to see this merged, as it directly solves an issue I ran into. That said, I completely understand that I’m just an external contributor and that maintainers have a broader perspective on the project. If you feel another approach is better, I respect that decision and appreciate you taking the time to consider this! Thanks again for your work on this project! 🚀

> The current fix has downsides:
> 
> * silent swallowing of potential errors makes debugging hard
> * removing fix is backwards compat breaking
> 
> Considering that the bug is for a very specific use case, I'd prefer an alternative design where we introduce a `sendThinking` (or similar) model option that defaults to true. When false, no thinking is forwarded.

Done. One note, the `signature: part.signature!` build-time assert in conversion is knowably not always valid at runtime, e.g. the example in this PR where we use middleware to extract `thinking` tags and there is no accompanying signature data. Even if one could view this as a provider-side model issue as a non-reasoning model is outputting `thinking` tags.

This makes me still wonder if we should also omit if signature is nullish, since it is in violation of the request spec.

We can consider the above for a later change as the current one is opt-in and addresses the immediate issue.

body: This seems overly specific for the examples. What would the impact be for other proxy or deployment setups?
author: lgrammel

body:
@lgrammel 

In many implementations of Server-Sent Events (SSE), it's important to disable certain types of compression (e.g., gzip) to ensure that the event stream is delivered correctly and in real time.
When compression is enabled, some proxies or intermediaries may buffer or delay the response until they have enough data to compress, which defeats SSE’s purpose of sending data as soon as it is available.
By using the header "Content-Encoding: none," you explicitly tell the server and any intermediaries not to apply any compression, ensuring that each event is transmitted immediately and maintains the proper SSE format.

- This is a problem that developers frequently encounter in various scenarios where compression is enabled.
- Adding this header helps developers spend more time solving these common problems.
- This declaration is only valid for this stream API and will not affect other API endpoints.
- I think I can remove the word "nextjs" and only keep the word "compress middleware.". Make it more common, not for some specific framework.

more info:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29807834/express-js-not-streaming-chunked-text-event-stream-resposne

To keep track, here are the methods that were previously sync and are now async:

- `processResult` in `packages/ai/core/generate-object/generate-object.ts`
- `validatePartialResult` and `validateFinalResult` in `packages/ai/core/generate-object/output-strategy.ts`
- `parsePartial` and `parseOutput` in `packages/ai/core/generate-text/output.ts`
- `transform` in `packages/ai/core/generate-text/stream-text.ts`
- `parsePartialJson` in `packages/ai/core/util/parse-partial-json.ts`
- `onToolCallDeltaPart` in `packages/ai/core/util/process-chat-response.ts`
- `doGenerate` and `doStream` in `packages/amazon-bedrock/src/bedrock-chat-language-model.ts`

body:
I've reviewed your PR at a high level and have 2 fundamental concerns:

1) The PR includes prompt modifications, something we try to avoid having in the AI SDK (with very minor exceptions).
2) Longer term, the AI providers will move towards stronger tool call support, rendering this middleware unnecessary or even counter-productive (see e.g. https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/gpt4-1_prompting_guide#tool-calls ).

That said, it is very valuable to have this middleware today, and I realize that the prompt modifications are fundamental to its functionality. My suggestion would therefore be to publish the middleware as a standalone npm package in a repository that you own. We are happy to include a link to your package from the middleware page, please file a PR for the docs change when ready.

body:
### Explanation:
When I run `pnpm prettier-fix`, Prettier automatically removes quotes from object keys like `'o3'`, converting them to `o3`. This creates inconsistencies with other object keys like `'o3-2025-04-16'`, which must remain quoted for correct formatting and readability.

This configuration update will affect multiple files, so I will need to carefully manage and commit these changes.

### Screenshots for context:
![Screenshot 2025-04-25 194853](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffc4885b-92f2-4c02-98c6-7f96e2681929)
![Screenshot 2025-04-25 194756](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d80501dc-f776-4e9b-ba94-bad75ca68218)  

To address this issue, I updated the `prettier` configuration in `package.json` to set `quoteProps: "consistent"`. This ensures that object keys are consistently quoted. That is, they will either all have quotes or none, based on the context. This change preserves the quotes for keys like `'o3'`, keeping them consistent with keys like `'o3-2025-04-16'`.

### Configuration Change:
```json
"prettier": {
  "quoteProps": "consistent",
  "tabWidth": 2,
  "useTabs": false,
  "singleQuote": true,
  "arrowParens": "avoid",
  "trailingComma": "all",   //  changes
  "plugins": [
    "prettier-plugin-svelte"
  ],
  "overrides": [
    {
      "files": "*.svelte",
      "options": {
        "parser": "svelte"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

With this change, Prettier will now keep object keys consistently quoted, preventing the inconsistencies and ensuring uniform formatting across all keys. that way the many file change.

After making these changes, I ran `pnpm prettier-fix`, which resulted in multiple files being updated.


### Screenshots for context:  
![Screenshot 2025-04-25 201534](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/611192e6-0c88-4253-b2be-808d8c521950)  

![Screenshot 2025-04-25 201650](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae14a694-6340-4e0d-8cff-05cb2a6ce839)

Yep I was unsure on the best way to approach this problem. The issue is what if it throws it inside the stream, so it ends up being serialised as a data stream message - in that case what is the best way to surface the error message to the user. ```
Unknown chunk type: source-url at Object.transform
  (file:///[obscured]/node_modules/ai/core/generate-text/stream-text.ts:1516:21)

Simply searching this of `type: 'source-url'` and `type: 'source'` (also with double quotes) I find many different cases of places where this new pattern might not have been impemented.

This happens in `stream-text.ts`, it doesn't seem to properly handle a `source-url` type, but also documentation, some tests and some other cases haven't been converted properly yet. Feel free to research out if I could help out with fixes these.

body:
One problem we ran into is that the JSON schema created by `z3.object()` and `zod-to-json-schema` differs from `z4.object().toJsonSchema()`

`zod-to-json-schema` seems to set `"additionalProperties": false,` by default on objects. z4's `.toJsonSchema()` does that only for `z4.strictObject().toJsonSchema()`

At least for OpenAI, the missing `"additionalProperties": false` causes an error:

> Invalid schema for response_format 'response': In context=(), 'additionalProperties' is required to be supplied and to be false.

`z4.strictObject()` is equivalent to `z4.object().catchall(z.never())`

I opened an issue for `zod` to discuss how this could be solved: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/4498

**Update:** resolved via https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/4498#issuecomment-2905616731

body:
Hey - Super keen to start using this so I've been poking around, figure I'll offer my 2 cents

You appear to have two causes for the recursive type error, the first https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/bca63f96a0a7e85a9f713d8d371abf8182fcb682/packages/ai/core/tool/mcp/types.ts#L20

Is because when `TOOL_SCHEMAS = 'automatic' | undefined`, the second branch is continually taken, as when it recurses it recurses with `TOOL_SCHEMAS = Record<string, { parameters: ToolParameters<unknown> }>` which is invariant to `Record<string, { parameters: ToolParameters<any> }>`... and so the second branch is taken again, infinitely recursing

I think this is as simple as switching both tool schema records to use unknown?


I'm not so sure about the second one: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/7324c21294042983f930f400d3466b3468d0f788/packages/ai/core/generate-object/stream-object.ts#L165 (identical to the other file).

I think it's because you are defining `RESULT` before `SCHEMA`, even though it depends on schema, which is triggering re-evaluation? in combination with the large union of any zod3 object & any zod4 object? I think your comment on the zod repo will yield much clearer answers.

Regardless, I have a fix. By pulling out some of the heavy lifting into helper types:

```ts
type InferSchema<S> =
  S extends z3.Schema ? z3.infer<S> :
  S extends z4.$ZodType ? z4.infer<S> :
  S extends Schema<infer T> ? T :
  never;

type InferFor<S, O extends 'object' | 'array'> =
  O extends 'array' ? Array<InferSchema<S>> : InferSchema<S>;
```

You can write the signature like:

```ts
...
export async function generateObject<
  SCHEMA extends z3.Schema | z4.$ZodType | Schema = z4.$ZodType<JSONValue>,
  Output extends 'object' | 'array' | 'enum' | 'no-schema' =
      InferSchema<SCHEMA> extends string ? 'enum' : 'object',
  RESULT = Output extends 'array' ? InferFor<SCHEMA, 'array'> : InferFor<SCHEMA, 'object'>
>(
  options: Omit<CallSettings, 'stopSequences'> &
 ...
 ```
 
 So that the generics are in order
 
 
 ---
 
Hopefully this is both clear & helpful, apologies that the explanation of the second issue is a bit fuzzy

body:
Left some reviews. It's *extremely* thoughtful to try to ensure compatibility with Zod 3.24.x, to put it nicely. Based on a quick scan, the current implementation will not work well for 3.24.x - I explain more in my reviews.

You're going to have a much easier time if you bump your Zod peer dep to 3.25. The timing with `ai@5` works out great for this. There are zero breaking changes from 3.24 -> 3.25 for Zod 3 users. It's just a matter of running `npm upgrade`. 

Arguably, a minor version bump in a peer dependency does not qualify as a breaking change at all since (assuming the peer dependency library didn't break anything between minors) it requires no code changes on the part of your users. 

Note also I plan to publish `zod@4` on npm at some point. At this point, the `"zod"` package root will start exporting Zod 4 instead of Zod 3. Zod 3 will then only be available at `"zod/v3"`. This will require more code changes on your end and make it infeasible to support Zod 3.24.x. This may happen sooner rather than later.

PS Gregor - feel free to DM me about this stuff. I'm not on mastodon but I am on X/Bsky 👍

body:
This means you now always need to call `createUIMessageStream` if you want to persist messages.

I don't like the direction `ai` is taking, I don't want to call `createUIMessageStream`, I want to implement my own serialization (or use the RSC format directly with the async iterator created by `streamText().fullStream`), `ai` now requires you to always create a `UIMessageStream` instead of working with the result of `streamText`. 

An `UIMessageStream` is yet another stream format added to the package when we already have the one from `streamText().fullStream` which people already know. Why add yet another one?

What I would like to see instead is for these features to not require the `UIMessageStream` serialization:
- Convert response messages to `UIMessage` for persistence
- Emit custom data parts from tools `execute`

This could be done by 
- supporting generators in the tools execute functions, yielded items will simply become items in `streamText().fullStream`
- keeping `appendResponseMessages` or something similar
- adding a function `messagesFromfullStream` that creates an `UIMessage` from a `streamText().fullStream` (now this function requires an ui stream instead of the result of `streamText().fullStream`, when both formats are basically the same thing)

body:
@lgrammel I gave what you were saying some thought and revamped the PR to keep the `useChat` API exactly the same. The only difference now is that the `Chat` class from the React package is now the "container" for subscriptions rather than the `AbstractChat`. The major benefit of this is that `AbstractChat` is no longer multimodal / leaky as an abstraction -- it uses the `ChatState` abstraction passed to it and doesn't have to worry about _also_ firing events. This will prevent bugs in the future where we remember to call `pushMessage` but forget to emit an event, or vice versa.

(In reality there's really no difference in functionality whatsoever here -- previously, the "subscriber" logic lived on `AbstractChat`, and now it lives on `Chat`, which extends `AbstractChat` in the first place. The way that API is _expressed_ has changed a little bit, but the functionality has not.)

The only downside to this is that the `Chat` class now has a `~register*Callback` function on it for each of the three types of state. I prefixed it with that for the same reason the folks over at StandardSchema did: Because it sorts it to the bottom of the autocomplete list. The only reason they're necessary at all is because React needs some place to "anchor" state invalidations within `useChat`, and `useSyncExternalStore` is that "anchor" position. 

Overall this feels like a much better separation of concerns -- React keeps all of the React-y things contained in the React package, and the core package just says "hey, update your state like this!"

body:
Hey @lgrammel! I might have mentioned the problem in the previously closed PR [here](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5626#issuecomment-3019062084).

But in short, Google APIs only support a subset of OpenAPI schema and `additionalProperties` is not mentioned as one of the supported ones, ref: https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#FunctionDeclaration

The proper handling for `additionalProperties` should be to remove them and not add them to the converted schema, similar to what langchain does in their [implementation](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchainjs/blob/451f4568d6f66d8feeeb79aa414bb41a8b913373/libs/langchain-google-genai/src/utils/zod_to_genai_parameters.ts#L26-L57).

This PR builds on top of @tjenkinson's PR where he made the change to recognise objects with `additionalProperties` as non-empty object. That is crucial because otherwise you incorrectly remove them from the converted schema.

body:
@lgrammel Nope, as google decided to not follow the standard JSON Schema conventions. For example `const` is not supported for zod literals, instead having to convert them to an enum with one single value. 

Regarding recurrent JSON schemas, normally `$ref` and `$defs`/`definitions` are used but Google decided not to follow that standard and use `ref` and `defs` (without the dollar sign) instead, so we need to convert the standard openapi schema into google's stupid version.

My biggest concern is how to model different image editing operations going forward, and whether to have a single generate or more specific functions.

E.g. typical operations are to edit images, enlarge images, generate image variants. All of these would fall under edit. While this may not be relevant for the openai image api, there are many other image APIs that we will need to support.

What are your thoughts on this? how would this work with other image generation APIs?
author: lgrammel

body:
> My biggest concern is how to model different image editing operations going forward, and whether to have a single generate or more specific functions.

Thanks for the review @lgrammel. I appreciate you taking the time to look at this even during the v5 Beta. 

You ask a great question. I'm not too attached to this implementation, but here are my thoughts:


### Why as part of Generate Image

Fun fact, on the first iteration, instead of `generateImage`, I created an `editImage` function + a  `doEdit` method in the image model. However, I changed to the current implementation for the following reasons:

- Realized that "edit image" is just "images used as input" (together with a prompt). This is not too different from how the "generateText" can use images with a prompt.... Just different outputs.
- I liked the simplicity and consistency of `generateText`, `generateImage`, `generateSpeech`

### Compatibility of other providers

I agree that integrating functionality from many providers is a challenge. Not sure how to solve this. 

Let's consider a small example from Luma ["Generate an Image"](https://docs.lumalabs.ai/reference/generateimage):

The Generate Image endpoint has the parameters: "image_ref", "style_ref", "character_ref", and "modify_image_ref".

The question (IMHO) is not if these are image generations or image edits. Rather, how do we present parameters that are useful for some providers but not for others? 

I can think of the following options:
1. No validation: We use optional properties, and we let the API respond with an error when they are not allowed
2. Validate on the model: We validate them inside each image model and respond with a nicer error (at more development cost)
3. Typesafe params: we change some of the Call Options based on the model selected (like a discriminated union). 

I like option 3 and find it similar to the `ProviderOptions` approach. However, maybe 1 or 2 are better in the short term

body:
**Description**

**Problem**

When the Vercel AI SDK is configured with `providerOptions` to pass resources (such as `file_ids` for the `code_interpreter` tool), it automatically adds a `tool_resources` object to the request body. That is the standard and expected format for the OpenAI Chat Completions endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`).

However, our project uses the beta endpoint `/v1/responses`, whose request schema is different and **does not** accept the `tool_resources` parameter. As a result, every call failed with **400 Bad Request** and the message “Unknown parameter: 'tool\_resources'”, preventing us from sending files to the Code Interpreter. The `/v1/responses` API expects `file_ids` to be passed directly inside the tool’s own `container` object.

**Solution**

To fix this incompatibility in a robust, maintainable way—without editing the library inside `node_modules`—we implemented a **“controlled fork”**:

1. **Custom class**
   We created `custom-openai-responses-language-model.ts`, which defines a `CustomOpenAIResponsesLanguageModel` class—a controlled copy of the original `OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel`.

2. **Payload transformation**
   In the custom class, the `doStream` and `doGenerate` methods intercept the request body before it is sent to OpenAI and:

   * Move `file_ids` from `body.tool_resources.code_interpreter.file_ids` to `body.tools[...].container.file_ids`.
   * Remove the `tool_resources` key entirely from the final request body.

3. **Provider integration**
   `openai-provider.ts` was updated to import and instantiate `CustomOpenAIResponsesLanguageModel` instead of the default class, ensuring every `openai.responses()` call uses our custom transformation logic.

This approach restores compatibility, keeps project code clean and isolated from third-party dependencies, and safeguards our implementation against future Vercel AI SDK updates.

@gabrielsch I also added an example in examples/next-openai to help, but this branch is functional in v5

> > > This feel somewhat complicated to me. Is the new openai reasoning test at the heart of the issue?
> > > It is slightly complicated since the LangaugeModelV2 interface only allows for reasoning to be a string, whereas OpenAI has an array of summary strings... For multi-turn conversations and in general, generateText and streamText should give you the exact same output format so you can mix these and they construct message chains correctly. OpenAi emit the correct encrypted content for stateless reasoning at the end of all delta streams, so you need to await and send reasoning end with updated metadata when this happens.
> 
> my thinking was that it can be sent as part of the reasoning end. let me give it a quick try, will build on this later today

yes i do send it at reasoning end now, but when I spoke to OpenAI engineers yesterday, they also say that for some users it make sense to have encrypted content on the reasoning start too, to kind of prepare UI or whatever that something is coming here, even though that encrypted content is not complete until the one you receive at reasoning end. That is why I added it at two places to be 100% correct with OpenAI spec and what the engineers said.
The problem you will run into is that you want to emit deltas, and you have to start a new reasoning item before you can finish the old one, because OpenAI will emit the correct encrypted content in the end, whereas streaming summaries arrive before, and we want to relay as much as possible of that to the user of the API, and not accumulate and stop streaming in the OpenAI provider before we emit. I could not come up with another solution than this one. The tests showcases how I envision it should work. Main point is that streamText and generateText should generate the same set of objects for multipart reasoning, and that is where we have the bug today. The dont do that.

I have updated all the test mocks so they correctly describe a real OpenAI response in these cases.

body: Yes. I want to decorate these functions with extra parameters and logic, and it is a mess with the types, so I thought it would help others to have this possibility. My concrete use case is to expose for example generateText to other developers (we are a big team), forcing them to pass usage analytics parameters. Then the middleware automatically adds and configures an analytics service and attaches it to whatever languagemodel the developer is using. Lint rules then forbid the import from vercel ai sdk, but instead to these decorated functions. The developer can use the vercel ai sdk as usual, but is required to pass an extra object that configures everything and keeps everything dry. Every call needs a new set of parameters which is why the provider registry or provider doesnt work.

body: The solution with provider options seems wrong to me. We have provider defined tools in the AI SDK. Is there a way to solve this without providerOptions?
author: lgrammel

body:
> The solution with provider options seems wrong to me. We have provider defined tools in the AI SDK. Is there a way to solve this without providerOptions?

Thanks for the feedback!
Some third-party proxy platforms (outside official/community providers) only work through @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, and their tools format can differ from the standard.
Currently, providerOptions.tools gets overridden by the request’s tools, so provider-specific tools can’t be preserved.
I used providerOptions here as the smallest, backward-compatible fix.
If you’d prefer a dedicated merge mechanism in the core, I’m happy to adjust this PR in that direction.

body:
>  isn't this expected behavior? you never fully consume the stream, so onFinish is not called, since you may continue consuming the stream at any point

That is currently not possible with the current implementation. A for await creates a new iterator each time, but that iterator calls stream.getReader() which fails if the stream is still locked by the previous loop. You would need to add `releaseLock` to add support for that case

I think cancelling the stream when you exit the for loop is the better interface. Otherwise it is too easy to create memory leaks where you never consume the stream when using await for.

Do you want me to add more tests for that file in this PR?

body:
Some things that were not clear while implementing this, and should be clarified before resuming this PR

- In this PR I tried handling error that happen in the middle of the stream. This is supported only for a few model providers like Anthropic, OpenAI and others instead don't support resuming an assistant message. Instead other providers can only resume a stream at step boundaries (after tool call end, or start of stream). This needs to be handled, probably only resuming at last step instead of middle of text like it does now
- In this PR I am blocking the sending of error, finish and finish-step parts because these should not appear in the response in case of a retry. This made logic very complex and difficult to follow. An alternative way to do this should probably be used

> revert all the nullish changes and the docs changes

@lgrammel fair enough. 

Just a note though - since these schema's are only used in this function, and the validation function is only exported as a **nice-to-have**, there's not much reason to block the support of a wider range of falsy/nullish scenarios on set properties.

I'd argue the utility of the function is just to validate the bare minimum requirements for a `UIMessage` to _display_ it's necessary information, which is in most cases just the `type` and then the messages core information given its state.

The omitted/undefined/nullish/falsy scenarios for properties kind of becomes unimportant at that point, which then questions the utility of this function if its going to throw errors unless all the aforementioned property scenarios are coerced to `undefined`.

body:
## 🔧 Fixed the Empty Provider Labels Issue

Thanks for the excellent review feedback @vercel! I've addressed the critical issue where the workflow would fail with an invalid JSON Schema when no provider labels exist.

### Changes Made:
- ✅ **Added empty labels detection**: Check if provider labels array is empty in the fetch step
- ✅ **Conditional AI classification**: Only run `vercel/ai-action` when provider labels exist
- ✅ **Updated all conditions**: Added `has-labels` checks to all dependent steps
- ✅ **Added fallback comment**: Inform users when no provider labels are configured yet

### How it works now:
1. **When provider labels exist**: Works as before with AI classification and labeling
2. **When no provider labels exist**: Skips AI step and adds a helpful comment explaining the situation

This prevents the JSON Schema validation error from `"enum": []` and makes the workflow robust for repositories without provider labels configured yet.

The workflow is now safe to deploy and will handle edge cases gracefully! 🚀

It seems like these recurring bugs are all symptoms of a deeper architectural mismatch between the SDK's universal format and Anthropic's uniqlue API, which has led to a cycle of "band-aid" fixes.
 
For what it's worth, I believe the only permanent solution would be to evolve towards a provider-specific "builder" pattern that constructs a compliant payload from the start. This is similar to the more direct and stable approach that is already used successfully in the Google provider's conversion logic.
​Adopting this pattern for Anthropic would likely eliminate this entire class of bugs and pay down the accumulated technical debt.
