body:
This looks great—thanks for working on it. I wanted to share a few thoughts after experimenting with different approaches to tool approval and complex tools with the AI SDK.

## Approval use cases

When thinking about tool approval, two use cases come to mind:

1. Getting authorization from the user (tool: send_email)

- This is the simple case. The UI shows a dialog with the LLM‑suggested inputs. If you want to go deeper, you can allow the user to edit the inputs, and then approve or deny. This can be conditional, depending on tool inputs and program context; for example, if the email is to a domain different from the user's and the user is not an admin, require approval. (The AI SDK has what we need via `experimental_context` (or roll your own `AsyncLocalStorage`), and we have the inputs and callbacks (`onInputAvailable` and `execute`).)

2. Setting up program state so that the tool has the required prerequisites for execution (tool: read_calendar)

- A function receives the input and context and determines whether we already have the OAuth scopes. If we do, no approval step is required. Otherwise, it generates a URL that the user can use to grant the scopes. Ideally, this is passed as metadata so the UI can properly guide the user through the approval process.

Example workflow with general approach of this PR:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram

participant AI
participant AISdk
participant ComplexTool
participant UI
participant User

AI->>AISdk: read_calendar(input)
AISdk->>ComplexTool: [needsApproval callback]
alt requiresApproval
    ComplexTool->>AISdk: { requiresApproval: true, meta: { oauthUrl: "https://..." } }
    AISdk->>UI: { type: "tool-approval-request", ..., meta: { oauthUrl: "https://..." } }
    UI->>User: Take user through OAuth flow
    User->>UI: Approved: finished OAuth flow
    UI->>AISdk: { type: "tool-approval-result", ..., approve: true, meta: { oauthUrl: "https://..." } }
else
    ComplexTool->>ComplexTool: { requiresApproval: false }
    AISdk->>ComplexTool: execute(input)
    ComplexTool->>AISdk: result
    AISdk->>AI: result
    AISdk->>UI: { type: "tool-output-available", ..., output: result }
    UI->>User: Show result
end
```

Without making `needsApproval` a callback and being able to provide custom metadata, it's hard to build more complex interactions like the one above.


## Alternative idea

Overall, the AI SDK is really powerful, but the part that doesn't expose enough is tool execution. We have hooks like `onInputAvailable`, `onInputDelta`, and `onInputStart`, but we cannot affect the tool (`input`, `execute`, etc) or the program flow (`streamText`) based on these callbacks like we can with `prepareStep`. If we want to handle tool execution ourselves, we need to drive the whole loop manually, which makes using the UI message stream and other features harder.

A different, more extensible future:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram

participant AI
participant AISdk
participant ComplexTool
participant UI
participant User

AI->>AISdk: read_calendar(input)
AISdk->>ComplexTool: [prepareTool callback] We don't have the OAuth scopes,
ComplexTool->>ComplexTool: { toolExecution: { stopReason: "approval", meta: { usefulToUI: "require_oauth", oauthUrl: "https://..." } } }
AISdk->>UI: Update `part.type` to `tool-approval-request` with metadata returned by the tool
AISdk->>AISdk: Stop `streamText` loop
UI->>User: Complex interaction happens
UI->>AISdk: { type: "tool-approval-result", ..., approve: true, meta: { calendarId: "123" } }
AISdk->>ComplexTool: [prepareTool callback] OK, let's override our input (return it) { execute: async (input, opts) => ..., input: { ... } }
```

The current `needsApproval: boolean` can be implemented by adding a `prepareStep` that returns `toolExecution: { stopReason: "approval" }`.

This approach aims to:

- Allow tools to return data to the UI that does not go to the LLM (`meta`). This is currently not possible unless you hack the `onFinish` callback (piggybacking on `tool-input-available` `providerMetadata`):

```typescript
        onFinish: (stepResult) => {
          if (stepResult.finishReason === "tool-calls") {
            for (const entry of stepResult.content) {
              if (entry.type === "tool-call" && entry.input && !entry.providerExecuted) {
                writer.write({
                  type: "tool-input-available",
                  toolCallId: entry.toolCallId,
                  toolName: entry.toolName,
                  input: entry.input,
                  providerMetadata: {
                    ...entry.providerMetadata,
                    app: {
                      waitingForApproval: true,
                      // Used by the UI to render and validate a form
                      inputSchema: getToolInputJSONSchema(entry.toolName) as Record<string, any>,
                    },
                  },
                });
              }
            }
          }
```

- Allow the UI to provide custom data to stopped tool calls. Same as above but in the other direction, the only way to do this now is handling tool execution manually outside of `streamText`, like the [existing example](https://ai-sdk.dev/cookbook/next/human-in-the-loop).

- Stop the `streamText` loop when the tool definition determines it should be stopped for various reasons (e.g., approval). Currently, the only way to do this is by not providing an `execute` function on the tool, which cannot easily be done conditionally.

Overall there's a need for tools to be "stopped" for various reasons approval being the most common one. But approval can be very complex like requiring a user to grant OAuth scopes, dependant on input, program context, timeout, resource availability, etc. Perhaps thinking about tools being in a "stopped" state for various reasons is a better way to think about it.

body:
> can you share why this is needed? I looked through https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/structured-output, and I understand what it does, but what is the use case for it?

Because LLMs generate things token-by-token the generation of every token is affected by every previous token. That means that in structured outputs it is important to specify the order of the properties. For example: You are creating a CoT pipeline and have defined the following structure:
```
reasoning: z.array(z.string()),
result: z.string()
```

Then you always want the llm to generate the 'reasoning' property first, and the 'result' property last.

This is a really important feature for many use cases in more or less complex AI pipelines used in production.
author: NikitaHerndlhofer
gr2m

body:
@gr2m 
Because the json deserialization does not keep the property order you should really have a look at the raw generated response of the llm, I think it's the ```result.response.body```.
Look at the specific order, then set the ```propertyOrdering``` setting and look how the property order changed.

It's easier when you name your properties like
```
propertyOne
fieldTwo
attributeLast
number5
```

Then the lllm will be more inconsistent in the result.

So the best way to test this would be:
1. Set a defined seed
2. Set temperature to 0
3. Run the inference
4. look at the property order
5. Set a different propertyOrder setting
6. Run the generation again and compare the results

body:
Hi Will, thanks for creating this pull request!

We currently don't have specifications for video models, so a Twelve Labs provider isn't feasible yet. While we've explored video functionality with fal.ai and Google Vertex, we haven't prioritized this work due to the significant investment required. Video's large file sizes present unique challenges that would necessitate new APIs for features like async handling.

We're interested in understanding your vision for Twelve Labs + the AI SDK. What advantages would an AI SDK provider offer compared to using your twelvelabs-js SDK directly? We'd be happy to discuss this further on a call if you prefer.
author: gr2m

body:
@gr2m This is James from the TwelveLabs team. Thanks for the thoughtful reply — that makes perfect sense.

Our main motivation for proposing a TwelveLabs provider is to make multimodal (especially video) understanding as accessible as text and image models already are in the AI SDK. TwelveLabs’ API already supports async workflows and chunked video processing, so our integration could help validate a video provider spec within the SDK without requiring major backend changes right away.

From our perspective, the key advantages of adding TwelveLabs as a provider are:

- **Unified developer experience**: Developers using Vercel’s AI SDK could query TwelveLabs models the same way they query text or image models (via `streamText` / `generate`), without installing another SDK.
- **Next.js-native multimodality**: Many Next.js apps are evolving toward rich media inputs — e.g., video search, summarization, and content generation. A TwelveLabs provider would show how video understanding fits naturally into that workflow.
- **Early spec collaboration**: We’d be happy to help shape and test the SDK’s video provider spec — using TwelveLabs as a reference for async ingestion, status polling, and response streaming.

Totally understand that video support isn’t prioritized yet, but even a “non-standard experimental provider” path would help the ecosystem move toward that goal.

This is [my Calendly](https://calendly.com/james-le-twelve-labs) if you want to do a short call to explore how we could help prototype this without creating long-term maintenance overhead.
author: james-le-twelve-labs

body:
Thanks for the feedback @lgrammel! I've updated the PR to use intermediary proxy callbacks in `useChat`. This ensures the `ai` package is not modified and all changes are now isolated to `@ai-sdk/react`.

The callbacks ref is updated on each render, and the wrapper functions passed to the Chat instance read from this ref, so they always use the latest user-provided callbacks without needing setter methods on `AbstractChat`.

body:
@lgrammel  Correct me if I'm wrong but this seems incorrect. `structuredOutputs` wasn't replaced with `strictJsonSchema`, `strictSchemas` was. And the real breaking change is that it now defaults to false instead of true.

It is also more nuanced than that since `strictJsonSchema` is a new property for chat models (which also defaulted to true, just without a property to change it to false), whereas it is a rename of `strictSchemas` for responses models.

Moreover, responses models always defaulted `structuredOutputs` to true, even in 4.0. In v5, both chat and responses default structuredOutputs to true.

So structured outputs migration is confusing on multiple dimensions: responses vs chat models, property renames, different property defaults... _and_ the new default API is now responses instead of chat when calling the plain `openai()` function. Massive 🤯.

I think the migration doc should also emphasize that this _will_ break structured outputs and to preserve v4 behavior, `strictJsonSchema` should be set to `true`. In fact, I'm not quite sure what the use case for `strictJsonSchema: false` even is in the context of the AI SDK, since the Zod schema validation will be strict _regardless_, and it will throw an error if the non-strict openai response doesn't match, which is likely.

body:
@valenradovich unfortunately it is not as straight forward afaik, bc translation also depends on e.g. provider options (see openai responses provider) and the system prompt (and how it is included). i understand the use case, trying to figure out an elegant solution here.

Brainstorming here
- Model classes would need to have an optional async function that supports converting to some sort of mode specific format. Alternatively this could be docoupled into standalone functions (maybe better)
- That conversion function would need to be standardized
- A common function in AI could take a prompt (incl. system and provider options) and a function and resolve this.

Something like

```ts
const apiMessages = convertToApiMessages({
  model: LanguageModelV3 | string, // or apiConverter: function(LanguageModelV3Prompt + providerOptions) => unknown
  prompt: string | ModelMessage[],
  system: string;
  providerOptions
})
```

Other options may be important as well though

body:
> > Could affect generate/stream text/object url downloads
> 
> I confirmed that it e.g. applies to this example, without a way to set a max download size.
> 
> ```ts
> await generateText({
>     model: openai('gpt-4o'),
>     messages: [
>       {
>         role: 'user',
>         content: [
>           { type: 'text', text: 'Describe the image in detail.' },
>           {
>             type: 'image',
>             image:
>               'https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/examples/ai-core/data/comic-cat.png?raw=true',
> 
>             // OpenAI specific option - image detail:
>             providerOptions: {
>               openai: { imageDetail: 'low' },
>             },
>           },
>         ],
>       },
>     ],
>   });
> ```
> 
> should we add `maxDownloadSizeInBytes` to all the methods exported by `ai` that might do downloads?

Adding maxDownloadSizeInBytes to all methods breaks encapsulation regarding download configuration and leads to unspecified behavior with custom download functions.

instead I'd prefer if we could expose our download function somehow, with the max download size as an option (but there will be a naming conflict with the upcoming download for the files api that we need to solve).
users can then choose custom download functions (our download function configured with a different limit) and the concepts stay clearly separated.

Thanks for the question!

As far as I know, after you obtain the `file_id` from the AI SDK you need to call Anthropic’s Files API directly to download the file.

Here are examples that only use `generateText` / `streamText`:

- `examples/ai-core/src/generate-text/anthropic-code-execution-20250825-downloads.ts`
- `examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/anthropic-code-execution-20250825-downloads.ts`

And here is a Next.js example:

- Next.js example  
  ```bash
  cd examples/next-openai
  pnpm dev
  # then open:
  # http://localhost:3000/chat-anthropic-code-execution
  ```

The downloading route is here:
`examples/next-openai/app/api/code-execution-files/anthropic/[file]/route.ts`

I’m not sure there is dedicated documentation for this flow yet, but I’m confident that you can implement file downloads for code execution results in your app using this approach.

Does this help answer your question? 🙂

body:
> I don't understand the premise of why this PR was created in the first place. `preliminary: true/false` is how you distinguish streaming from the final result. Can you show an example that does not work with the current implementation?

I am not the author, but for me relying on the `preliminary: true` value in a stream response seems like an anti-pattern. The AI SDK docs and AI Elements Tool component all use the tool state as the primary indicator of tool status, and this PR adds a proper state that applies to that pattern. Without it, I think all AI SDK users would have to build additional, custom logic to read a tool response for a preliminary value and handle it accordingly--this seems like the exact boilerplate the AI SDK tries to prevent.

Thanks I'll spare some time for updating to beta then.

As of today there's unfortunately one more complexity. Though not documented in https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1-for-developers/, based on curl testing, 5.1 actually support temperature and log_probs **if you use None as reasoning effort**.

body:
@gr2m / @dancer

this pr introduced a breaking change causing `vitest` to be loaded, breaking jest test suites running on commonjs.

error:

the test utilities in `provider-utils/dist/test/index.js` now bundle the test-server code, which results in hardcoded vitest imports

`var import_vitest = require("vitest");`

this causes an immediate failure when jest tries to load the module such as:

```
Vitest cannot be imported in a CommonJS module using require().
Please use "import" instead.
```

please consider decoupling vitest utilities from the general test utilities, as this allows package consumers to make their own decisions without being stuck on a particular version due to incompatibility with peer dependencies or frameworks chosen by your team

FWIW, its been easy to use the ai sdk thus far due to its low-dependency nature. adding stuff like this, along with msw, create tighter binds against the current ergonomics of using the library, which may not be what you want in the long run

body:
## **Summary of Substantive Changes since beginning of v5.1/v6.0 beta**

### **New Capabilities in v3:**
1. Document reranking model type (completely new)
2. Embedding model middleware system (completely new)
3. Structured warning types across the SDK

### **Type Safety Improvements:**
1. Headers type no longer allows `undefined` values
2. Required specification version fields for better version detection

<details>

### **embedding-model**
1. **doEmbed method signature refactored**: Changed from inline options object to extracted `EmbeddingModelCallOptions<VALUE>` type (better code organization)
2. **Headers type strengthened**: Changed from `Record<string, string | undefined>` to `Record<string, string>` (removed optional undefined values)

### **embedding-model-middleware**
- **NEW FOLDER** - Entire middleware system for embedding models introduced in v3
- Provides `transformParams` and `wrapEmbed` hooks
- Allows overriding provider, modelId, maxEmbeddingsPerCall, and supportsParallelCalls

### **image-model**
- No substantive changes (only type name updates)

### **speech-model**
- No substantive changes (only type name updates)

### **language-model**
- No substantive changes to the model interface itself (only type name updates)

### **language-model-middleware**
1. **Specification version field changed**:
   - v2: `middlewareVersion?: 'v2' | undefined` (optional for backwards compatibility)
   - v3: `readonly specificationVersion: 'v3'` (required and readonly)
   - **Impact**: All v3 middleware must explicitly declare their specification version

### **provider**
1. **New specification version field**: v3 requires `readonly specificationVersion: 'v3'` property
2. **New model type method added**: `rerankingModel?(modelId: string): RerankingModelV3` (optional)

### **reranking-model**
- **NEW FOLDER** - Entire reranking model type introduced in v3
- Provides document reranking functionality:
  - `doRerank` method
  - Supports both text documents and JSON object documents
  - Returns ranking with index and relevance scores
  - Optional `topN` parameter to limit results

### **shared**
2. **New warning type introduced**: `SharedV3Warning` with structured warning types:
   - `unsupported-setting` - for unsupported configuration settings
   - `compatibility` - for compatibility features that might be suboptimal
   - `other` - for general warnings
   - **Impact**: More structured and type-safe warning system

</details>

body:
Keeping track of what I've found

- `mode` was removed in #5580
- the `Respond with a JSON object` tool injection was removed in #5834

We need to figure out why we did that but I don't think we should bring back functionality that was removed as part of v5. If I recall correctly, we responsibility for the correct parsing was moved from the `ai` core methods like `generateObject()` into the providers. Could you review the PRs, I assume there are some clues in there.
author: gr2m

body:
The background and summary in https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5834 sum it up pretty well

> ## Background
> Almost all providers support structured output generation via JSON mode or JSON schema. The distinction between JSON and tool generation modes prevents streamlining flows and leads to additional calls when building remote providers.
> 
> ## Summary
> Always send JSON schema from `ai` to the providers when generating structured outputs. Push responsibility for prompt modification and forced tool usage (when JSON schema is not available) into providers.

So I'd to the following

1. We can close this PR
2. Create a separate PR that removes the `mode` types because it should have been removed as part of #https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/5580 already
3. Look into implementing the tool call for the provider that needs it, or ask users to do it for providers that need it, if there are only a few left. In which case I'd update our docs

body:
Thank you @gr2m for the details, I understand now that the `mode` parameter and tool injection were intentionally removed as part of the v5 architecture changes.

## Addressing Your Questions:
1. **Test snapshot changes** : These changes occurred because when no schema is provided, my implementation doesn't set `responseFormat`.
2. **Tool injection concern**: You're absolutely right - this was the v4 approach that v5 intentionally moved away from. The responsibility should be in the providers, not in the core.

## The Real Fix:
The issue #10023 should be fixed in the provider packages **@ai-sdk/groq** and **@ai-sdk/google**, Should detect when JSON mode + schema conflicts and fall back to tool calling

I agree with your recommendation to close this PR, Thanks for letting me work and for knowledge, I am new to Open source and open source contribution and this helped me understand it (they are not like any "good first issue" kinda contributions)

body:
hey @felixarntz, after the above request changes, I did tried this approach - Instead of guessing automatically, expose a provider option that lets the user explicitly choose the strategy.

`structuredOutputMode` supports:
1. `auto/native` (default)
Use native structured output (responseSchema / json_schema) — identical to current behavior.
2. `jsonTool`
Replace the response format with the synthetic JSON tool. This is intended for models that reject schema+tools.

But I still have multiple open question and other 2 approaches that i didn't specific choose but still want to confirm with maintainers.

I can give a detailed comment here but is there a better communication channel like discord or slack or community (i can create new topic there), etc. 

#### not pushed this approach, but all test passes, still - From my perspective, this approach is the strongest choice because:

- It doesn't break any existing behavior (zero risk regression)
- It mirrors what the Anthropic provider does for the tool mechanics, so the patterns are consistent across the SDK
The isJsonResponseFromTool dynamic flag (computed from actual response, not config) correctly handles edge cases that a static flag misses — this is the same pattern Anthropic uses
- The Groq streaming restructure (deltas before finish-reason) fixes a real timing bug regardless of which approach is chosen
- The weakest point is that auto doesn't actually auto-detect, which means users still get the original #10023 error by default and need to discover the structuredOutputMode: 'jsonTool' option. 

That's why i have some questions that will fix this (may fix this).
author: Sahilbhatane

body:
@Sahilbhatane Ideally we align with the approach from #10502. What you're proposing is close to it, but not quite.

I think it's crucial that we're aware here which models support _actual_ structured output vs which do not - unless an entire provider doesn't support it.

While normally I would advise against specific model support maps like this, we're only building this JSON tool as a workaround, and in a perfect world it would never exist. Requiring the user to be aware of this low-level nuance would not be great DX, and that's why in the Anthropic provider there's also the awareness for whether a model supports structured output or not.

Please feel free to iterate on this PR. Also note this needs a refresh from latest `main`, as there are currently merge conflicts.
author: felixarntz

body:
@felixarntz updated based on your review feedback. here is what changed:

#### Approach:

- The synthetic JSON tool is now used strictly as a fallback, not as the default behavior. Native structured output remains the primary path.
- Added `structuredOutputMode` provider option (auto , `outputFormat` , `jsonTool`) for both Google and Groq, aligning with the Anthropic pattern from #10502.
- `getGoogleModelCapabilities()` / `getGroqModelCapabilities()` provide the model-awareness layer. Currently all models return `supportsStructuredOutputWithTools`: false since no Google/Groq model is documented to support `schema+tools` together. When models add support, these functions can be updated with model-specific checks (like Anthropic's `getModelCapabilities()`).

#### Activation logic: The JSON tool is injected only when ALL of these are true:

1. `responseFormat.type === 'json'` with a schema
Tools are present
2. The model does NOT support native `schema+tools` (per capabilities + `structuredOutputMode`)
3. When the JSON tool is NOT needed, the request is unchanged from current behavior (zero regression risk).

#### Bug fixes included:

Fixed a streaming bug in both providers where return inside the transform function would exit the entire chunk processing (skipping tool call conversion and finish reason), changed to continue (Google) / conditional wrapper (Groq).

Tests: 287 Google tests passing, 84 Groq tests passing. Two test cases added (auto fallback + `outputForma`t override) per provider. Happy to add more test coverage for streaming, explicit `jsonTool` mode, and response mapping if desired.

*and* : OpenRouter and AI Gateway (from the original issue #10023) are not addressed in this PR, just because they were out of scope

I also did AI review on change code for any fallbacks or error with cursor.

Oh, I see — the tests currently depend on a build step, so you need to run a build before executing them
(I’ve updated the reproduction steps above accordingly). Could you check if this works now?

## Additional thoughts on this
The CI handles this automatically via `turbo test`, which defines the following dependency chain:

```json
  "tasks": {
    ...
    "test": {
        "dependsOn": ["^build", "build"]
      },
    ...
  }
```

This is okay. However, AFAIK, Vitest can transpile source code on the fly — it doesn’t usually require a prebuild. But it seems this is not the strategy here.

What feels a bit odd is having to build every package just to test a single one. Technically, I could also build only the dependent packages, but that’s still quite tedious. At least with the build:packages filter, you can skip building the examples 😄

## CI Failures Investigation

I've investigated the failing checks and found that both failures are unrelated to the Streamdown migration changes in this PR:

### 1. TypeScript Error
- **Error**: `Cannot find module '@cfworker/json-schema'` in `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`
- **Root cause**: The dependency updated from `1.24.0` to `1.24.3` in the lockfile, and the newer version has different peer dependency handling
- **Verification**: TypeScript passes locally with the current lockfile
- **Status**: Appears to be a CI cache/environment issue

### 2. E2E Test Failures (`streamable.e2e.test.ts`)
- **Tests failing**: `createStreamableValue and readStreamableValue` and `test-streamable-ui`
- **Error**: Test timeouts - elements `#test-streamable-value` and `#test-streamable-ui` not found on page
- **Root cause**: The test server is failing to build with `Module not found: Can't resolve '@ai-sdk/rsc'`
- **Verification**: Same failures occur locally, even after building the package
- **Impact**: This PR doesn't modify any RSC code - only documentation and example files that use ReactMarkdown → Streamdown

Both of these issues appear to be pre-existing problems unrelated to the Streamdown migration. The PR changes are limited to:
- Documentation updates
- Example application UI updates (ReactMarkdown → Streamdown)
- Package.json and lockfile updates for the new dependency

None of these changes would affect the RSC package's internal tests or the TypeScript dependency resolution for MCP SDK.

body:
Adding a `foo: 'bar'` in openai image model provider metadata, before this change, running the `src/generate-image/openai.ts` example script and logging provider metadata gives:

```
Provider metadata: {
  "openai": {
    "images": [
      null
    ]
  }
}
```

After:
```
Provider metadata: {
  "openai": {
    "images": [
      null
    ],
    "foo": "bar"
  }
}
```

However, this change is still data-lossy in that we effectively apply "last one wins" to provider metadata fields other than `images`. We may make multiple image model requests when needed to generate more images than a provider can execute in one request. In this case we can end up with more than one `providerMetadata` in need of merging. For `images` we carefully preserve order and concatenate, but for the rest of the data we just merge as last-one-wins.

Sonnet 4.5 summary:

## The Challenge

When `generateImage` needs to make multiple calls to the provider (e.g., requesting 3 images but `maxImagesPerCall` is 2), the function must aggregate results from multiple provider responses. The key challenge is: **how should provider metadata be merged when each call returns its own metadata?**

## Current Merging Logic

Looking at lines 169-191 in `generate-image.ts`, the current logic:

1. **For the `images` field specifically**: Concatenates arrays to preserve order
   ```typescript
   if ('images' in existingMetadata && 
       Array.isArray(existingMetadata.images) &&
       Array.isArray(metadata.images)) {
     (providerMetadata[providerName] as { images: unknown[] }).images = [
       ...existingMetadata.images,
       ...metadata.images,
     ];
   }
   ```

2. **For all other fields**: Uses **last-one-wins** via object spread
   ```typescript
   providerMetadata[providerName] = {
     ...(existingMetadata as object),
     ...metadata,  // This overwrites any conflicting keys
   } as ImageModelV3ProviderMetadata[string];
   ```

## What This Means

**Images field**: Properly merged and order-preserved across calls ✓

**Non-images fields**: Last call wins. For example:
- Call 1 returns `{ routing: { provider: 'openai' }, cost: '0.04' }`
- Call 2 returns `{ routing: { provider: 'vertex' }, generationId: 'gen-123' }`
- **Result**: `{ routing: { provider: 'vertex' }, cost: '0.04', generationId: 'gen-123' }`

The `routing.provider` from call 2 overwrites call 1's value, but `cost` from call 1 is preserved since call 2 didn't include it.

## Potential Issues

1. **Semantic correctness**: If  a value differs between calls, the final metadata only shows the last value, losing the history
2. **Aggregatable fields**: Fields that one might want to sum are instead overwritten/lost
3. **Nested objects**: Deep merging doesn't happen—entire nested objects are replaced

## Test Coverage

The tests verify this behavior works as designed (see test cases starting line 665), but they don't explicitly call out the last-one-wins semantics for non-images fields. The tests show it working correctly for the gateway use case where later calls add new fields rather than conflicting ones.

**Summary for code review**: The current implementation uses last-one-wins for all non-images metadata fields. This works for the gateway's current usage pattern (where successive calls add complementary fields), but could lose information if providers return conflicting values for the same field across multiple calls.

I do not think input editing is a good idea because:

1) it changes the provider generated tool call args and some newer models do not allow this. i have already seen issues with repairing tool calls because of this

body:
Support + fresh verification data for this PR.

**Context (2026-04-20)**: Vercel's 2026-04-18 security bulletin referenced unauthorized access to internal systems; community reporting named npm publishing tokens among potentially compromised assets. Whether or not those specific claims hold, the coverage gap this PR closes becomes materially more valuable when the publishing-credential threat model is non-hypothetical.

**Current coverage gap (public registry metadata, 2026-04-13..2026-04-21)**:

| Family | attested | unattested |
|---|---:|---:|
| `next` + `@next/*` + ecosystem | 105 | 0 |
| `turbo` + `@turbo/*` + ecosystem | 44 | 0 |
| `vercel` CLI | 10 | 0 |
| `ai` | 0 | **42** |
| `@ai-sdk/openai` | 0 | **13** |
| `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | 0 | **15** |

Same `vercel-release-bot` publisher across both sets.

**Verified against pinned runtime (pnpm 10.11.0, npm 11.12.1)**:

I independently tested the exact diff in this PR against the pinned toolchain. Findings:

- `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true` (this PR's change) works as expected: `pnpm publish` invokes `npm publish <tarball>` internally; npm CLI reads the env var as a config override; combined with `permissions: id-token: write`, npm's OIDC handler at `lib/utils/oidc.js` fires, exchanges OIDC for an auth token, and `libnpmpublish` signs a Sigstore attestation.
- A commonly-proposed alternative, `pnpm_config_provenance=true` (lowercase, pnpm prefix), is a **silent no-op** on pnpm 10.11.0 — the publish handler never reads `opts.provenance`, only forwards CLI args to npm. Grep on the pnpm 10.11.0 bundle returns zero occurrences of `sigstore`, `OIDC`, or `attestation`.

This PR has the correct env var. The evidence file I generated is available on request.

**`git apply --check` against current HEAD**: exit 0. The 6-line diff still applies cleanly 4.5 months after submission.

Happy to see this merged as-is. PR #12241 (Trusted Publishing migration) is a natural follow-up but requires per-package npmjs.com admin action; this PR has no prerequisites and is safe to merge immediately.

/cc @tnkuehne — thanks for filing this back in December.

body:
> hi @akshayasana , we'll be closing this PR. although this approach works, ideally we want to have support for other providers that may support this fucntionality. and for that we have a different approach in mind.
> 
> would recommend keeping an eye on issue #11133

Thanks for reviewing this PR and pointing to [#11133](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/11133) - the file-reference approach makes sense for cross-provider file ID support.

That said, I wanted to share the thought process behind this PR in case it's useful:

The CustomPart addition for user message content serves as a general-purpose escape hatch, similar to how custom already exists in LanguageModelV3ToolResultOutput. The container_upload use case was just one example.

This pattern could be valuable for:
 - Stopgap for new provider features before SDK adds first-class support
 - Truly provider-specific features that may never have cross-provider equivalents
 - Rapid prototyping of new APIs without waiting for SDK releases

The two approaches seem complementary rather than mutually exclusive - file-reference for standardized cross-provider features, and custom as an escape hatch for provider-specific edge cases.

No follow-up needed - just wanted to share the reasoning. Closing this PR, will keep an eye on the 11133.

body:
@Und3rf10w
activeTools doesn't work because I have many service-specific tools (Gmail, Jira, Slack, etc.).
The problem: Loading all tools upfront means paying for all their token costs in every request(the cached token costs are high on scale), even with activeTools filtering.
Why I need dynamic injection: Start with only toolSearch (minimal tokens) → discover and load only the tools needed for that request → only pay for what gets used.
Why not layered agents? Using separate agents for each service adds additional roundtrip latencies for delegation, making responses slower.
This makes it feasible to scale to dozens of tools without prohibitive token costs while keeping responses fast.

body:
I would love typebox integration (ideally via Standard JSON Schema), but I am wondering what else this provides:

- zod is already natively supported
- raw json schema is already supported via `jsonSchema()`
- valibot is already supported via `@ai-sdk/valibot`
- arktype is supported through standard json schema

Is there a way to have a more limited `@ai-sdk/typebox`? or is TypeBox standard json schema compatible?

I do not want to add more complexity for our users to understand. However, if direct typebox support is not possible, could this be a community maintained library (outside of `@ai-sdk/`) that we link to from our docs?
author: lgrammel

body:
@lgrammel Hi! Thanks for the review!

I’ll provide some additional info below, but I’m certainly open to thoughts on alternative designs if this PR is not a good fit. Regarding TypeBox though, this package would service as an integration path, but the package itself is more about improving the JSON Schema validation story in this SDK.

---

## TypeDriver Overview

> but I am wondering what else this provides:

This package is essentially a constrained version of the existing `jsonSchema(...)` function, but where validation happens exclusively through a JSON Schema compliant validator. It is written specifically to remove potential mismatches between schema representation, validation and type inference (which is currently possible with the existing `jsonSchema(...)` function)

```typescript
const A = jsonSchema({ type:'string' }, value => {  // schema: string
  return typeof value === 'number'                  // check:  number
    ? { ... }                                       // infer:  boolean ??
    : { ... }
})
                                                    // ensure consistency
                                                    // 
const B = schema({ type: 'string' })                // schema: string
                                                    // check:  string
                                                    // infer:  string
```

From a design standpoint, the implementation was written to try consolidate multiple schema definitions under the SDK’s `Schema<T>` structure. The ability to do this was facilitated by way of the new Standard JSON Schema specification.

> ⚠️ Note: Standard JSON Schema is "NOT" JSON Schema. TypeBox cannot implement on that basis.

| Input | Mapping |Output |
| ---      | --- | --- |
| JSON Schema | Implicit | `Schema<T>` |
| TypeScript | Parse Implicit | `Schema<T>` |
| Zod| Standard JSON Schema | `Schema<T>` |
| Valibot | Standard JSON Schema | `Schema<T>` |
| ArkType | Standard JSON Schema  | `Schema<T>` |

... and where the reduction to `Schema<T>` was somewhat considered against the current downstream type differentiation / inference handling observed below.

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/provider-utils/src/schema.ts#L63-L87

```typescript
// multi type differentiation 
export type InferSchema<SCHEMA> =
  SCHEMA extends ZodSchema<infer T>
    ? T
    : SCHEMA extends StandardSchema<infer T>
      ? T
      : SCHEMA extends LazySchema<infer T>
        ? T
        : SCHEMA extends Schema<infer T>
          ? T
          : never;
```

... which could simply be reduced to.

```typescript
export type InferSchema<SCHEMA> = SCHEMA extends Schema<infer T> 
  ? T 
  : never
```

... but where the package offers library integration (as before) + other features.

- Full support for Zod, Valibot, ArkType, Effect  (and TypeBox)
- Acceleration support for JSON Schema via Standard JSON Schema
- Internationalized Error Reporting (i18n support)
- and [more](https://github.com/sinclairzx81/typedriver?tab=readme-ov-file#Features)

## Standardized Validation

As noted above, the main intention here is to merely provide this SDK a means to validate data strictly in accordance with the JSON Schema [specification](https://github.com/json-schema-org/JSON-Schema-Test-Suite/tree/main/tests/draft2020-12) regardless of the underlying library or schema format.

```typescript
const A = schema(z.toString())       // Zod
const B = schema('string')           // TypeScript
const C = schema({ type: 'string' }) // JSON Schema

A.validate('foo')                     // uses JSON Schema validation !
B.validate('bar')                     // uses JSON Schema validation !
C.validate('baz')                     // uses JSON Schema validation !
```

The `@ai-sdk/typedriver` is designed to relinquish validation control away from each library and delegates it exclusively to a standards based validator (specifically one that can be verified for compliance with the JSON Schema specification via [automated testing](https://github.com/sinclairzx81/typebox/tree/main/test/jsonschema) - so TypeBox (or Ajv it doesn't matter which))

- [JSON Schema 2020-12 Test Suite](https://github.com/json-schema-org/JSON-Schema-Test-Suite/tree/main/tests/draft2020-12)

... and where the validator is guaranteed to return validation check results the same as any other validator that implements the specification.

- [Other Spec Compliant Validators](https://json-schema.org/tools?query=&sortBy=name&sortOrder=ascending&groupBy=toolingTypes&licenses=&languages=&drafts=&toolingTypes=&environments=&showObsolete=false&supportsBowtie=false#validator)

... and where the requirement to have consistent schema validation typically emerges in micro-service infrastructures where application domain models are shared between systems (as JSON) and thus need to be understood by each system equally.... (or data integrity hazards may result)

---

So, this package is attempting to solve a few "things" (where I think this package could provide some utility to other parts of the code base, at least in part), but the most pressing requirement for me would be the JSON Schema validation represented as a core feature of the SDK (especially as it relates to the MCP protocol)

With regards to a potential `@ai-sdk/typebox` package, this is possible of course, but I would much prefer to see a Ajv validator with a decent JSON Schema inference system behind it. 

As an alternative to this package, I would certainly be open to contributing a modern JSON Schema inference system for the benefit of this SDK should it decide to embrace standards compliant JSON Schema validation.

Cheers!
S
author: sinclairzx81

body:
@lgrammel Sorry, just to follow up on this aspect

> I would love typebox integration (ideally via Standard JSON Schema), but I am wondering what else this provides:

As mentioned, I can’t really support the specification in TypeBox, but I did want to raise the specification as a potential integration hazard waiting to happen. In order for this (or other) SDKs to receive a valid JSON Schema, the Standard JSON Schema specification would require JSON Schema to effectively invalidate itself....

As per the specification outline:

https://standardschema.dev/json-schema

> Standard JSON Schema is a common interface designed to be implemented by JavaScript and TypeScript entities that **"ARE"** or can be converted to JSON Schema.

... which is effectively asking JSON Schema to provide a redundant self referential adapter to itself (via invalid keyword)

```typescript
// Json Schema

const S = { type: 'string' }        // <-- also TypeBox type

// Standard JSON Schema

const S = {                         
  type: 'string',

  '~standard': {                    // Non-Standard (should be prefixed with `x-` fails Ajv)
    jsonSchema: {
       input: () =>                
        ({ type: 'string' }),       // Redundant Self Referential Meta Schema
       output: () => 
        ({ type: 'string' })        // Redundant Self Referential Meta Schema
    }
  }
}
```
And I am somewhat mindful of trying to mitigate a future where this could become a problem

```typescript
const A = Output.object({ type: 'string' }) // error: not Standard Json Schema ?

const S = { type: 'string' }

const B = Output.object({ ...S, '~standard': { jsonSchema: { ... } } }) // hmmm
```

I wouldn't expect many users to really know the difference between JSON Schema and Standard JSON Schema (so expect some confusion here), but in terms of using the specification as a direct integration device, I would approach with some care, particularly in light of a possible ....

[JSON Schema Standardization under Ecma International](https://github.com/orgs/json-schema-org/discussions/938)

---

All said, the `@ai-sdk/typedriver` package does provide some shielding against many of the inverted design aspects of the specification (as it would relate to JSON Schema specifically), but irrespective of this package, I would encourage a degree of care to ensure Standard JSON Schema doesn't end up hindering plain JSON Schema compatibility with SDK interfaces down the line....

Native TypeBox compatibility would largely depend on the SDK accepting plain JSON Schema as an input format.

## Model Capability Fixes

I've pushed a commit to fix incorrect capability flags for Together AI and Fireworks models in the provider comparison table.

### Changes Made

| Provider | Model | Object Gen | Tool Usage | Tool Streaming |
|----------|-------|:----------:|:----------:|:--------------:|
| Together AI | `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo` | ❌→✅ | ❌→✅ | ❌→✅ |
| Together AI | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-Turbo` | ❌→✅ | ❌→✅ | ❌→✅ |
| Together AI | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` | ❌→✅ | ❌→✅ | ❌ |
| Fireworks | `accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v3` | ❌→✅ | ❌→✅ | ❌ |

### Verification Sources

**Together AI** - The [official function calling documentation](https://docs.together.ai/docs/function-calling) explicitly lists all three models as supporting function calling:

> Together AI supports function calling for:
> - `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo`
> - `Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-Turbo`  
> - `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3`

**Fireworks** - The [DeepSeek V3 model page](https://fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/deepseek-v3) confirms:

> "Function calling (tool use) in JSON format, available on Fireworks' Serverless tier"

### Why Tool Streaming is ❌ for DeepSeek V3

Both Together AI and Fireworks documentation note that DeepSeek V3 has limitations with multi-turn function calling:

> "Multi-turn function calling is still an area of improvement"

To be conservative, I've kept Tool Streaming as ❌ for DeepSeek V3 on both providers while enabling the single-turn capabilities (Object Generation, Tool Usage).

If there is an approved client tool call that has not been executed (no tool result), the whole request is invalid. It should include the tool result. Thus there is an error with how the AI SDK is used. Filtering out the empty parts does not fix that, it hides the problem.

@aayush-kapoor 

## Addressing Review Feedback                                                                      
                                                                                                     
  Thanks for the thorough review! Here's a summary of all the changes made:                          
                                                                                                     
  ### 1. Changeset Description                                                                       
  Done  
                                                                                                     
  ### 2. CLI Examples                                                                                
  Added CLI examples at:                                                                             
  - `examples/ai-functions/src/generate-text/xai-mcp-server.ts`                                      
  - `examples/ai-functions/src/stream-text/xai-mcp-server.ts`                                        
                                                                                                     
  Also added Next.js example with multi-turn conversation support at                                 
  `examples/next-openai/app/chat-xai-mcp-server/`.                                                   
                                                                                                     
  ### 3. CI Test Failures                                                                            
  Fixed - all 142 tests pass (node + edge). The prettier warning on `dist/index.d.ts` is expected    
  since it's a generated file.                                                                       
                                                                                                     
  ### 4. server_label Optional                                                                       
  Fixed - `server_label` is now optional per xAI docs in both the schema and type definitions.       
                                                                                                     
  ### 5. Test Snapshot Changes                                                                       
  The snapshot changes show `text-end` events are now emitted immediately when message content       
  completes, rather than at the very end of the stream. This fixes duplicate text emission - the text
   block should signal completion when its content is done, not when the entire response finishes.   
                                                                                                     
  ### 6. Annotation Handling Logic                                                                   
  The annotation handling was moved to the `response.output_item.done` handler to ensure annotations 
  are processed when the message item completes. The xAI API delivers annotations on the done event, 
  so processing them there is more reliable.                                                         
                                                                                                     
  ### 7. ToolLoopAgent Pattern                                                                       
  Updated to use the ToolLoopAgent pattern:                                                          
  - Created `examples/next-openai/agent/xai-mcp-server-agent.ts`                                     
  - Updated route to use `createAgentUIStreamResponse`                                               
                                                                                                     
  ### 8-9. Multi-turn Conversation / Tool Name Mapping                                               
  Fixed the root cause. Added `mcpToolName` extraction and mapping in both `doGenerate()` and        
  `doStream()`:                                                                                      
                                                                                                     
  ```typescript                                                                                      
  const mcpToolName = tools?.find(                                                                   
    tool => tool.type === 'provider' && tool.id === 'xai.mcp',                                       
  )?.name;                                                                                           
                                                                                                     
  // In tool call handling:                                                                          
  } else if (part.type === 'mcp_call') {                                                             
    toolName = mcpToolName ?? part.name ?? 'mcp';                                                    
  }                                                                                                  
                                                                                                     
  This ensures tool names in responses match user-defined names, fixing multi-turn conversations.

body:
Hey @lgrammel  @michael-han-dev, I wanted to flag a backward compatibility concern that we experienced first-hand in production due to this changes.

When a new server (with this PR) sends responses to an old client (without this PR), the client fails to parse the streaming response.

The finish chunk format changes from:
{"type":"finish","finishReason":"stop"}
To:
{"type":"finish","finishReason":"stop","usage":{"inputTokens":10,"inputTokenDetails":{...},...}}

The issue is related to the use of z.strictObject() in languageModelUsageSchema, which rejects any object with unexpected properties or missing required keys. This strict validation causes old clients to fail when receiving the new streaming format.

This breaks rolling deployments where the server updates before all clients have refreshed their browser tabs. Users with stale frontend code will have their chat completely broken until they manually refresh.

I don't think this breaking change is intentional so pointing it out in case is useful. In our case our clients are already being force to update but would be good to address it for other users that have not updated yet.

body:
> The test does not fail without the fix, thus it does not reproduce the reported issue. I have reverted the fix to the production code and the test still passes.
> 
> It also uses real-time clock changes (delay) which must be avoided in unit tests, and could be simplified with DelayedPromise.
> 
> Can you simplify the test, avoid any delay/wait operations, and make sure it fails without the fix?

Simplified the tests with DelayedPromise and removed all delay() calls.

On the determinism issue: true race conditions are hard to reproduce in unit tests because JS is single-threaded - microtasks run sequentially even when promises resolve "simultaneously". The .finally() callbacks always execute one at a time, so the guard never gets exercised under normal conditions.

The new test triggers premature closure by using a constant generateId (which is what @convex-dev/agent does for message grouping - intentional on their side for thread message IDs, not a bug):
1. All tools add same ID to Set → only 1 entry
2. First tool completes → deletes ID → Set empty → stream closes
3. Other tools try to enqueue → throws without guard

Removing the if (!closed) guards produces:
TypeError: Invalid state: Controller is already closed

Vitest reports this as unhandled rejection and exits with code 1.

The generateId discussion is addressed in #11966 - it's being used for two purposes (message IDs vs tool execution tracking), and frameworks legitimately override it for message grouping.

I've been using Claude to help debug and write these fixes.

body:
> Hi @foontinz!
> 
> I came across this PR while trying to use partner models (like Kimi K2) on Google Vertex AI. This is exactly the feature I need.
> 
> **Use case**: I'm using Vertex AI with Kimi K2 models that require the `publishers/moonshotai` endpoint (e.g., `kimi-k2-thinking-maas`), which currently fails because the SDK hardcodes `publishers/google`.
> 
> The approach of parsing the publisher from the model ID (`moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking-maas`) is elegant because it:
> 
> 1. Maintains backward compatibility (existing `gemini-2.5-flash` calls still work)
> 2. Allows mixing models from different publishers in the same provider instance
> 3. Follows a pattern similar to how other providers handle organizations/namespaces
> 
> I noticed the PR has merge conflicts. Would you like any help resolving them? This would be very useful for anyone wanting to use Vertex AI partner models.
> 
> Also, I wanted to mention that I originally considered an alternative approach of adding a `publisher` option to `GoogleVertexProviderSettings`, but your model ID parsing approach is more flexible since it allows using multiple publishers with a single provider instance.
> 
> Example of what this enables:
> 
> ```ts
> const vertex = createVertex({
>   project: 'my-project',
>   location: 'global',
> });
> 
> // Use Google's Gemini
> await generateText({ model: vertex('gemini-2.5-flash'), prompt: '...' });
> 
> // Use Moonshot's Kimi in the same provider
> await generateText({ model: vertex('moonshotai/kimi-k2-thinking-maas'), prompt: '...' });
> ```
> 
> Thanks for working on this!

body:
Unclear to me if this should be added to `tool` or to `streamText/generateText` `timeout`.

If we think about who configures the timeouts and who writes the tool, I am leaning towards the latter for the following reason:

Assume 2 roles: tool user and tool author. they may or may not be the same person/group (e.g. for tools distributed as npm packages)

With the current approach, a tool user would need a wrapper tool to set the timeout on 3rd party tool. Also timeouts would get distributed into tools, vs being defined for a specific call.

Would be good to talk offline about the design but that was the reason why I postponed looking into this.

body:
My current attempt is to simpy use ToolLoopAgent in a step function. 🙈

```ts

export async function chat(writable: WritableStream<UIMessageChunk>, messages: UIMessage[]) {
  'use step';
  const agent = new ToolLoopAgent({...});
  const stream = await createAgentUIStream({
    agent,
    uiMessages: messages,
  })
  await stream.pipeTo(writable)
}
```

Streaming works fine and I can use it exactly like I'm used to.

DurableAgent has quite some limitations:
- Many details are implemented as very simplified stubs, such as the tool preparation which prevents using OpenAI provider tools.
- The default downloader doesn't work because fetch is blocked (need to use their fetch step function instead) and supportedUrls is empty.
- Model has to be provided as step function, therefore requires extra layer / provider wrapper packages. Custom provider registries are harder to use.
- Message metadata is a lot harder to add, requires disabling default start/finish chunks and sending them separately.
- ...

But of course, it has benefits. As far as I understood:
- Can resume multi-step calls instead of repeating from scratch. Not sure what happens if an error occurs mid-step (e.g. network failure) - will probably run that step again, but what about the already sent chunks?!?
- Tool calls are steps, so they can also be retried.
- Hooks can simplify human-in-the-loop / tool approvals.
- More stable environment for the loop controller.

Some ideas how similar features could be achieved in (a subclass of) ToolLoopAgent:
- Read back the stream to reconstruct the message chunks so far and continue from there. Or more abstract: Needs a way to "preload" the loop with the previously recorded intermediate step results and continue with the next step.
- AFAIU, calling a step function from another step has no special meaning, so no retries etc. That's only when they're called from a workflow function. Similar for hooks. Generally, ToolLoopAgent and the functions it calls are somehow orchestrating (like workflow functions), but they're far from just stitching steps together. That's why I think it makes sense to run them in a step function, but they could benefit from sub-steps. That needs further thoughts.
-  Of course, this assumes that the setup is still the same on the next retry, like all tools being defined in the same way, which seems to be guaranteed in the workflow VM. Then again, how big is the risk that this happens accidently and how big could the damage be?

I've put up a fix for this in #12664. The root cause is that `pruneMessages` doesn't track `caller.toolId` dependencies from `providerOptions` — when a child tool call references a parent via `providerOptions.anthropic.caller.toolId`, pruning the parent creates orphaned references that the Anthropic API rejects.

The fix adds transitive dependency resolution after computing the initial kept set, ensuring the full caller chain is preserved.

body:
Support for this Trusted Publishing migration.

**Context (2026-04-20)**: in the wake of Vercel's 2026-04-18 bulletin, removing long-lived npm publishing credentials from the workflow moves from "nice hardening" to "material posture change." This PR is the structural fix; PR #10773 (add `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE`, keep `NPM_TOKEN`) is the non-breaking immediate hardening. The two are complementary, not competing.

**Observation on the 50-package registration checklist in the PR body**: the checklist is the blocker, not the diff. `sibling org workflow vercel/turbo/.github/workflows/turborepo-release.yml` already operates under this pattern (publisher on npm = `GitHub Actions <npm-oidc-no-reply@github.com>`). The precedent is inside the org.

A safer rollout sequence, if the team wants it:

1. Merge PR #10773 first (provenance via classic token, no prereqs) → breach window gets a detection baseline immediately.
2. Begin per-package Trusted Publisher registration on npmjs.com (the checklist in this PR body) → can happen in parallel with #10773 in production.
3. Merge this PR only after registration is complete for every package.

If registration is partial at the time of merging this PR, un-registered packages fail publish with `Unable to authenticate, need: Basic, Bearer.` (confirmed in pnpm / npm CLI source). No atomic rollback. A pre-merge `verify-trusted-publishers.sh` preflight is worth considering; I have a draft available if useful.

`git apply --check` against current HEAD: exit 0. The 48-file diff still applies 2.5 months after submission.

/cc @gr2m — thanks for the comprehensive registration checklist; it's the right shape for this migration.

author: buibaoanh

body:
From a user perspective:

### Step 1: Tool Call Generation (Output)
**(i) What I put in:** A `generateText` call using `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` with a Gemini 3 thinking model.

**(ii) What I get back:** The reasoning state is returned under `providerMetadata: { vertex: { thoughtSignature: "..." } }`.

**(iii) Expected behavior:** Per [Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/thought-signatures), the `thoughtSignature` is a native field of the Gemini Part object. It should be returned under the `google` namespace to maintain consistency with the Google AI provider and allow for universal history persistence.

### Step 2: Tool Result Resumption (Input)
**(i) What I put in:** I pass the history back to the Vertex provider. Following the standard convention, the signature is provided under the `google` namespace.

**(ii) What I get back:** A 500 Internal Server Error from Vertex AI.

**(iii) Expected behavior:** The model should resume reasoning.

If user set `providerOptions` with key `google`, let's say `thinkingConfig`, right now what I got is `vertex` in `providerMetadata`.

I would expect `google` in `providerMetadata` as stated in [Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/thought-signatures) and for consistency reason.

_I noticed that `providerOptionsName` is selected by hardcoded provider Name for `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` instead of provider key in `providerOptions` in [this logic](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts#L100-L102)._

body:
Hey, @aayush-kapoor thanks for shipping this! We've been using it in production via a backport patch to v3.

One thing we noticed: `convertToOpenAIResponsesInput` includes the compaction block alongside ALL preceding conversation items. Per the [OpenAI docs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/compaction#latency-optimization):

> After receiving output items, you may optionally drop items preceding the most recent compaction item to reduce request size.

Without dropping preceding items, the full conversation is still sent as input on subsequent turns, so input token counts don't decrease even though compaction fires. The compaction blob is produced and round-tripped correctly, but the cost savings don't materialize because the API still bills for the full input.

Should `convertToOpenAIResponsesInput` detect the most recent compaction item and omit preceding messages? Or is that intentionally left to the caller?

body:
Thanks for the review! Addressing each point:

1. **Array.isArray guard** — `providerOptions.anthropic` comes from AI SDK's `SharedV3ProviderMetadata` type, constructed internally by the SDK. It won't be an array.

2. **Object.hasOwn** — `Object.entries()` already only iterates own enumerable properties. It does not traverse the prototype chain, so `Object.hasOwn` is redundant here.

3. **Reserved key conflicts** — The openai-compatible provider spreads `providerOptions.openaiCompatible` without reserved key checks either. This is developer-controlled input; if someone passes `role` or `content`, that's on them. Keeping behavior consistent with the existing pattern.

4. **`satisfies Partial<...>`** — `satisfies Partial` provides no meaningful constraint on an object literal with a spread. The current `as` cast is sufficient and consistent with patterns elsewhere in the codebase.

5. **Documentation** — Agreed, can be added as a follow-up.

6. **Performance / break early** — Assistant blocks typically contain 1-2 messages (the SDK merges consecutive assistant messages into one block). No meaningful optimization opportunity here.

body:
Thanks for the review! For more context on the RFC specifics, see the linked issue #12799.

To clarify: the issue isn't that `/` is forbidden in User-Agent headers generally — `curl/8.x` and `Mozilla/5.0` use it correctly as the product/version separator. The problem is that the SDK puts `/` **inside the product name token** itself.

Per [RFC 9110 §5.6.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-5.6.2), a `token` is `1*tchar` and `/` is not a `tchar`. The `/` is only valid as the separator between product name and version:

```
# Valid — "/" only as product/version separator
curl/8.11.1
Mozilla/5.0

# Invalid — "/" inside the product name or version token
ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.15   → product="ai-sdk", version="provider-utils/4.0.15"
runtime/bun/1.3.9              → product="runtime", version="bun/1.3.9"
```

Azure OpenAI enforces this strictly, but it's technically valid behaviour on their part. Other strict HTTP validators (curl `--head`, some load balancers) would also reject it.

@lgrammel Sure, I'll have a look. You're referring to https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/tool-loop-agent, https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/reference/ai-sdk-core/create-agent-ui-stream etc.?

Currently I don't see any examples for neither `onFinish` nor `onStepFinish` there, but I can add one showing the differences between adding them to either the `ToolLoopAgent` constructor or `createAgentUIStreamResponse` (e.g. for `useChat` from AI Elements).

But maybe these tables is even more helpful to understand my intention. This is the current situation:
| Callback | `ToolLoopAgent` constructor | `createUIMessageStream` | `createAgentUIStream` etc. |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| `onFinish` | `OnFinishEvent` (`ModelMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) |
| `onStepFinish` | `OnStepFinishEvent` (`ModelMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnStepFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) | `OnStepFinishEvent` (`ModelMessage`-based) ❌ |

And I think it should be:
| Callback | `ToolLoopAgent` constructor | `createUIMessageStream` | `createAgentUIStream` etc. |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| `onFinish` | `OnFinishEvent` (`ModelMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) |
| `onStepFinish` | `OnStepFinishEvent` (`ModelMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnStepFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) | `UIMessageStreamOnStepFinishCallback` (`UiMessage`-based) ✅ |

That gives devs the capability to hook into either the low-level part with `ModelMessage` or the higher-level with `UIMessage`. For `onFinish`, that is already implemented, but `onStepFinish` isn't consistent with that.

body:
Can you address these, in particular 1, 2, and 4.

We have skills specifically for agents in our repository, make sure your agent uses them.

### 1. Breaking change: Default filename loses .pdf extension

When no explicit filename is provided for a PDF file, the default changes from part-${index}.pdf to part-${index} (no extension).

- Chat completions: convert-to-openai-chat-messages.ts:137 (on main, line 131)
- Responses: convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts:142 (on main, line 139)

If OpenAI uses the filename extension for type detection (in addition to the MIME in the data URI), this could break existing PDF handling for users who don't pass an explicit filename.
Even if OpenAI currently uses the data URI MIME, this is a subtle regression that could surface unexpectedly.

Suggestion: At minimum, derive a sensible default extension from the MIME type (e.g., application/pdf → .pdf, text/plain → .txt), or keep the .pdf extension for the PDF-specific case.

### 2. Audio files silently sent as input_file on the Responses path

The Responses path (convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts) has no audio/* handling. Before this PR, sending an audio file would throw UnsupportedFunctionalityError. After this PR, audio
files would silently be routed as input_file, which is almost certainly wrong — OpenAI's Responses API likely expects audio in a different format (analogous to input_audio in chat
completions).

This means audio/wav, audio/mp3, etc. would now produce confusing API-level errors instead of a clear SDK-level error, which is a worse developer experience.

Suggestion: Add an explicit audio/* check in the responses path — either handle it correctly or throw UnsupportedFunctionalityError as before.

### 3. Error message change (minor breaking)

The error message for URL-based file parts in chat completions changes from 'PDF file parts with URLs' to 'file parts with URLs'. While the error class (UnsupportedFunctionalityError) is
  unchanged, anyone matching on the error message string would break. This is a minor concern but worth noting.

### 4. Missing changeset

Per the repo's contribution guidelines, every PR modifying production code needs a changeset. No .changeset/*.md file is included in this PR.

### 5. File ID detection inconsistency (pre-existing, but now more impactful)

The chat completions path uses hardcoded part.data.startsWith('file-') for file ID detection, while the responses path uses the configurable isFileId(part.data, fileIdPrefixes). This
inconsistency existed before but was limited to PDFs. Now that it applies to all file types, the divergence is more significant. Not a blocker for this PR, but worth flagging.
author: gr2m

body:
Thanks for the detailed review! I've addressed issues 1, 2, and 4 in the latest commit (048b876):

**Issue 1 — Default filename loses extension:** Fixed in both paths. Default filename now derives the extension from the MIME type using `mediaTypeToExtension()` from `@ai-sdk/provider-utils`, so e.g. an `application/pdf` file without an explicit filename becomes `part-0.pdf` instead of `part-0`.

**Issue 2 — Audio silently sent as input_file on Responses path:** Fixed. Audio file parts on the Responses path now throw `UnsupportedFunctionalityError` with a clear message, consistent with the behavior before this PR and matching how unsupported types are handled elsewhere in the SDK. This prevents confusing API-level errors.

**Issue 4 — Missing changeset:** Added `.changeset/fix-openai-input-file-audio-filename.md` with a `patch` bump for `@ai-sdk/openai`.

---

Regarding **Issue 3** (error message wording change from 'PDF file parts with URLs' to 'file parts with URLs'): this is intentional — the URL restriction applies to all file types, not just PDFs, so the updated message is more accurate. Happy to revert if you'd prefer to keep the original for back-compat.

Regarding **Issue 5** (file ID detection inconsistency between chat and responses paths): agreed this is a pre-existing inconsistency worth cleaning up, but I'll leave it as a follow-up since it's not introduced by this PR.
author: sleitor

body:
Fixed in commit 1fcc155.

**Test failures (VADE bot):** Five tests expected bare `part-N` filenames but the fix for issue #1 now derives the extension via `mediaTypeToExtension()`. Updated all five tests to match:
- `application/something` → `part-0.something`
- `application/pdf` → `part-0.pdf`
- `text/plain` → `part-0.plain`

**Issue #3 — Error message change:** The change from `'PDF file parts with URLs'` to `'file parts with URLs'` is intentional — the function now handles all media types generically, so the narrower PDF-specific message would be misleading. Anyone catching on the message string would need to update (the error class is unchanged), but this is consistent with the behaviour change. Happy to restore the old message if you prefer.

**Issue #5 — File ID detection inconsistency:** The chat path hardcodes `startsWith('file-')` while the responses path uses the configurable `isFileId(data, fileIdPrefixes)`. Fixing this properly requires adding a `fileIdPrefixes` option to `convertToOpenAIChatMessages` and threading it through the language model — happy to do that in this PR or a follow-up, whichever you prefer.

body:
Follow-up refresh is now pushed on head `b00621859`.

I re-ran the exact request-body proof on the rebased branch and compared it against current `main` using the real provider request paths (`doGenerate()`), not just helper-level tests.

Result on the refreshed branch: nested `oneOf` is converted to `anyOf` before send on all six active surfaces touched by this PR:
- OpenAI chat structured output: `response_format.json_schema.schema`
- OpenAI chat tools: `tools[0].function.parameters`
- OpenAI responses structured output: `text.format.schema`
- OpenAI responses tools: `tools[0].parameters`
- Anthropic structured output: `output_config.format.schema`
- Anthropic tools: `tools[0].input_schema`

Current `main` still sends raw `oneOf` on all six of those same surfaces, so the fix is still live and not upstream-absorbed.

Focused validation on the refreshed branch was clean twice with no code changes between passes:
- `pnpm exec ultracite check packages/provider-utils/src/convert-oneOf-to-anyOf.ts packages/provider-utils/src/convert-oneOf-to-anyOf.test.ts packages/provider-utils/src/index.ts packages/openai/src/chat/openai-chat-language-model.ts packages/openai/src/chat/openai-chat-prepare-tools.ts packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-prepare-tools.ts packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-prepare-tools.ts`
- `pnpm --dir packages/provider-utils test:node -- src/convert-oneOf-to-anyOf.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir packages/openai type-check`
- `pnpm --dir packages/anthropic type-check`

The only contributor-side fallout the refresh exposed was test-only: Unicorn's `no-thenable` lint rule now flags the JSON Schema regression case that uses a literal `then` property. I fixed that in `packages/provider-utils/src/convert-oneOf-to-anyOf.test.ts` by switching the setup to `Reflect.set(schema, 'then', ...)`, which preserves the exact schema coverage without changing production logic.

Temporary probe files used for the request-body proof were removed afterward, and both local worktrees are clean again.

body: @sleitor IMHO we should get rid of the `getAudioFormat` helper all together and pass all audio as `input_audio` (instead of file). That would align with how images and video parts are handled, which don't check against a list of supported formats. It also requires less maintenance when upstream providers add more supported formats over time.
author: heiwen

body: @heiwen Great suggestion! Applied in the latest commit — removed the `getAudioFormat` helper entirely and now pass all audio parts as `input_audio` regardless of format. The `format` field is derived directly from the media type subtype (e.g., `audio/ogg` → `ogg`), and URL data is passed as-is in the `data` field. This aligns with how image parts work and avoids maintaining a hard-coded allowlist as providers add new formats.

body:
@aayush-kapoor Thanks for the feedback! I understand the concern about the reproduction not matching the "normal" model sequence.

The fix addresses a real invariant imposed by the Anthropic API: when an assistant turn contains both `server_tool_use` (web_search/web_fetch provider-executed tools) and regular `tool_use` blocks, Anthropic requires the `server_tool_use` blocks to appear **before** any `tool_use` blocks in the content array. If the ordering is wrong, the API rejects the request with a 400 error.

The reproduction in issue #13013 does construct this sequence (a web_search tool alongside a regular tool call), and while the exact reproduction might be an edge case in typical usage, the underlying ordering constraint from Anthropic is documented and real. The fix is a targeted sort that only applies when both tool types coexist in the same assistant message, so it has no impact on the normal single-tool-type case.

Happy to adjust the approach if there's a better way you'd like to handle this constraint — but I'd argue the fix is correct even if the reproduction is unusual.

body:
@aayush-kapoor Understood — will update the test to use the actual raw API response from the Anthropic model rather than a manually constructed fixture.

Here's the actual scenario that triggers the issue:

**Prompt:** `Search the web for the latest news about AI SDK, then call my custom tool`
**Tools:** `web_search` (enabled via `betas: ['interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14']` or via the web\_search builtin) + a user-defined `custom_tool`

The Anthropic API returns an assistant message whose `content` array looks like:
```json
[
  { "type": "server_tool_use", "id": "srvtoolu_01...", "name": "web_search", "input": {...} },
  { "type": "web_search_tool_result", "tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01...", "content": [...] },
  { "type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01...", "name": "custom_tool", "input": {...} }
]
```

When this is sent back as the assistant turn for a second user message, Anthropic returns:
`400 Bad Request: tool_use block at index 2 must come after user's tool_result block for tool_use id "toolu_01..."`

Without the fix, `convertToAnthropicMessagesPrompt` preserves the original ordering, placing `server_tool_use` (with its `web_search_tool_result`) before `tool_use` — and Anthropic expects `tool_use` to appear before `tool_result`.

I'll update the PR with a test that records the actual API response (using a fixture captured from a real Anthropic API call) to make the reproduction more transparent. Let me know if you'd prefer a specific format for that.
