body:
Fixed in commit 3395a1f. Two changes:

- Polling loops replaced with bounded loops (300 attempts/600s for image, 500/1500s for video) with a timeout error on expiry.
- Image model was returning `outputs.map(url => ({type: 'url', url}))` which violates `ImageModelV4Result.images: Array<string> | Array<Uint8Array>`. Fixed to return `pollResult.outputs` directly (already `string[]` from the Zod schema).

body:
`[agent]`

**Agent:** Claude Code (`claude-opus-4-8`)

Hi @nicoalbanese 👋 — when you have a moment, would you mind taking a look at this entry?

It adds **Nimble** as a search-provider tool, mirroring the already-merged Tavily (#10567) and Exa entries in shape:

- One object appended to `content/tools-registry/registry.ts` — nothing else changed.
- `@nimble-way/ai-sdk` is published on npm (`v0.1.0`); the `codeExample` uses the current `isStepCount` API and a string model id.
- Checks are green (Socket Security + Vercel Agent Review); the deploy check is the external-contributor auth gate, not a build failure. Commits are signed/verified.

`nimbleSearch()` runs a live web search and returns ranked results (title, URL, snippet, full page content) for the model to ground a cited answer.

Thanks for maintaining the registry — happy to adjust anything you'd like shaped differently.

If you'd rather skip all updates until the next major or minor version, let me know by commenting `@dependabot ignore this major version` or `@dependabot ignore this minor version`. You can also ignore all major, minor, or patch releases for a dependency by adding an [`ignore` condition](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/configuration-options-for-dependency-updates#ignore) with the desired `update_types` to your config file.

If you change your mind, just re-open this PR and I'll resolve any conflicts on it.

body:
This lands the core shape I was looking for: resolve the approval lifecycle across the whole transcript before filtering any single message.

The remaining edge I would pin before merge is the unresolved approval-id case.

Right now the global approvalId lookup fixes the normal split-message path, but if an approval response has no matching request, or the request points at a toolCallId that cannot resolve to a tool name, the approvalId maps to no tool name. In selective pruning by tool name, that can turn into an implicit keep because the unresolved name is not in the pruned tool list.

I would make that branch explicit:

1. If the approvalId resolves to a pruned tool name, drop the response.
2. If the approvalId resolves to a surviving tool name, keep the response.
3. If the approvalId cannot resolve to any tool name, either drop it when pruning approval parts or surface a structural warning, but do not silently preserve it as authority context.

A small regression for a response with no matching request would close the loop nicely.

Boundary: architecture and regression-test feedback only; no claim about using this project or running its code.
author: rpelevin

body: Good fix! Moving the tool name resolution from per-message to across all messages is the right approach. The regression test with both tools and approval flow is thorough — covers the exact scenario from the issue. The changeset is clean too.

body:
Pushed a fix commit: the automated cherry-pick used `createProviderExecutedToolFactory`, which doesn't exist on `release-v6.0` (it was introduced on `main` after this branch was cut), so the build/type-check would fail.

Swapped it to `createProviderToolFactoryWithOutputSchema` — the same factory the sibling `parallel_search` / `perplexity_search` gateway tools use on this branch. On v6.0, provider-executed tools are represented purely via `type: 'provider'` (there's no `isProviderExecuted` flag yet), so this is behavior-equivalent.

Verified locally: `@ai-sdk/gateway` type-check passes and all 417 node tests pass.

body:
Gentle bump on this — I've filed #16695 to track the underlying bug with full reproduction steps, since there was no existing issue for it.

Quick recap: with access-token auth (non-Vercel environments), `resumeSession()` calls `Sandbox.get({ name })` without forwarding `token`/`teamId`/`projectId`, so `@vercel/sandbox` falls back to OIDC and resume fails. This PR forwards the credentials in `resumeSession()` and the snapshot polling path, with a regression test and changeset.

Happy to rebase or adjust anything if needed. cc @felixarntz @gr2m (recent committers on `sandbox-vercel` — apologies for the ping, tag whoever is more appropriate).
author: doneumark

body: Gentle bump — re-verified the bug is still present in `@ai-sdk/sandbox-vercel@1.0.24` (published today): `resumeSession` still calls `Sandbox.get({ name, signal })` without `token`/`teamId`/`projectId`, so access-token resume still fails with the OIDC error (#16695 has the full repro). Branch is current with `main` and mergeable.
